Procedure for Preliminary Enquiry
Upon receipt of Accident Report, the concerned Director/Departmental Head, along with relevant personnel from the department, shall conduct a preliminary enquiry to evaluate and determine immediate corrective action and long term preventive action and advise the concerned vessel accordingly in a prompt manner and if required, to all vessels of the group with a copy to the DPA. The proposed corrective and preventive action shall be reviewed by the concerned DO and approved by the DPA. The DPA shall advise the concerned department to issue Fleet Circular (Guidelines or Case-Studies) to the entire fleet, if considered necessary.
Where it is urgently necessary to mitigate the effect of a marine casualty or marine incident and to avoid recurrence, the concerned departmental head shall exercise due diligence to advise the vessel regarding immediate corrective action to be taken on board the vessel. The departmental head shall follow up this advice regarding immediate corrective action with an advice regarding long-term preventive action as described above.

Procedure for Independent Investigation
Upon receipt of report of major or catastrophic incident, the concerned Director/Departmental Head shall ensure that a preliminary enquiry is conducted in accordance with the procedure laid down in 9.3.1. A copy of the report of preliminary enquiry shall be forwarded to DPA.
The need for independent investigation, apart from above-mentioned preliminary enquiry, shall be decided by DPA in consultation with the Chairman and Managing Director (C&MD).

Investigating Team
Where it has been decided to conduct an independent investigation in accordance with 9.3.2 the DPA, in consultation with the departmental heads, shall constitute an Investigating Team. The Investigating Team shall jointly have adequate knowledge and experience of ship operations, technical management, operational management, safety management, required rules and regulations related to ship and marine industry. Members of the Investigating Team shall be independent of the area of investigation. However, the DPA may co-opt concerned person(s) from the area of investigation to the Investigating Team in order to provide specific inputs for the independent investigation from evidence obtained during the preliminary enquiry. | Procedure for Preliminary Enquiry

Non-conformity, Accident, Near Miss & Hazardous Occurrence | 
The Investigation team shall have a nominated team leader. Company encourages on job training for the investigation team members towards them getting familiarised with investigation issues.
The Investigating Team shall submit their report within the agreed time to the DPA. The DPA shall review the report of the Investigating Team and submit the same to the C&MD. Copies of the report of the Investigating Team shall be provided to the concerned ED/SVP and Director, upon instructions of the C&MD.

As far as practicable, the report shall be of confidential nature and shall be used only by the Company in aiding the implementation of preventive and corrective actions for such incidents. The report shall not be available to any outside party unless otherwise directed by the C&MD.

Investigating Team shall make every effort to ensure that the investigation report is unbiased and on basis of factual evidence, witnesses‘ statement of facts, interviews, records, photographs (if available), third party reports (if any), log book entries, supporting drawings/ plans and other available information. Investigating Team may also refer to available industry guidelines and procedures related to casualty investigation and preparation of reports. DPA, if required, shall advise the concerned department for issuance of fleet circular (Guidelines/ Case-Studies) based upon the outcome of investigation report.

Focus of the independent investigation shall be to ascertain the underlying causes and to recommend corrective and preventive actions.

9.3.4	FSI, GI & PSC Inspections & RCA
Vessels shall be put up for Flag State/PSC/GI Inspections as per DGS/IMO Guidelines. Master, in consultation with the operating division, shall plan and prepare the vessel for the FSI with due notification to the agents at the port of call towards co-ordination/liaisoning.
Vessels in foreign ports are subjected to PSC Inspections by different inspection regimes, such as Indian Ocean MOU, Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU, Mediterranean MOU, AMSA, USCG etc.
The vessel shall remain in readiness for such inspections with an aim to have minimum deficiencies. The inspection reports shall be forwarded to the operating division and ISM Cell along with the root cause analysis of the deficiencies. In case of detention, the operating division shall inform the DGS within 24 to 48 hours, followed by the corrective action and root cause analysis of such deficiencies.

PSC inspection deficiencies may be considered as non-conformities and corrective/preventive action shall be taken.

Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
For all accidents, near miss situations, non-conformities and PSC/FSI deficiencies/ detentions, root cause analysis shall be carried out for identifying direct, indirect and the root causes, by the concerned superintendent, which shall be submitted to concerned Group I/C | The Investigation team shall have a nominated team leader. Maintenance
Maintenance Policy, Maintenance Standard & Maintenance Responsibilities Maintenance Policy
It is the policy of the Company to carry out periodic and timely maintenance of all vessels in order to ensure:
that all Classifications & Statutory requirements are complied with,
that applicable codes, guidelines and standards recommended by IMO, Administration, Classification Society and other Maritime Industry Organisations are taken into account,
that vessels perform at optimum efficiency in a cost effective manner.

The implementation of the maintenance policy is achieved by providing to each vessel
duly trained, experienced and certified officers and staff capable of carrying out running and maintenance of all the machinery and equipment on board in a cost effective and safe manner.
spares, stores and other equipment essential for maintenance
necessary technical expertise and shore based assistance as and when the need arises.
information through technical bulletins, feed back of vessel‘s reports and parameters, minor alterations and retrofit for better efficiency of various equipment based on research and development.
in order to achieve the foregoing, the Company shall harness modern technology and latest techniques, where necessary.

Maintenance Standards
Maintenance Standards shall be based on:
Compliance with applicable rules and regulations and industry guidelines
Company's specific requirements
Manufacturer's guidelines (procedures) and periodic service bulletins for ship-specific equipments
Classification Society requirements
Administration, IMO, Port State Control, and other Maritime Industry Organisation requirements
Ship specific requirements.

Maintenance Responsibility
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the planned maintenance schedule is drawn up to suit the requirements of the vessel covering all machineries and equipments. These procedures shall be followed in order to have adequacy of maintenance as per standards mentioned in section 10.1 above. Delegation of jobs and responsibilities for maintenance shall be in accordance with maintenance responsibility under SMS Section 3 Procedures described herein will serve as guidelines and reference to the shipboard personnel to develop the planned maintenance system. | Maintenance

Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the planned maintenance schedule is drawn up to suit the requirements of the vessel covering all machineries and equipments. These procedures shall be followed in order to have adequacy of maintenance as per standards mentioned in section 10.1 above. Delegation of jobs and responsibilities for maintenance shall be in accordance with maintenance responsibility under SMS Section 3 Procedures described herein will serve as guidelines and reference to the shipboard personnel to develop the planned maintenance system.

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Guidelines on Planned Maintenance

General
Planned maintenance is aimed to achieve the following goals:
Safety, quality and efficiency.
Phased and balanced overhaul schedules.
Prevention of breakdown machinery/equipment.
Maintaining critical equipments/systems to their specified competency standards.
Optimisation of manpower, machinery and cost.
Control of spare parts and stores inventory on board.

Standard Maintenance Scheme
The Standard Maintenance Scheme shall cover:
Protective, Preservative and Predictive maintenance schedules.
Lubricating Schedules.
Schedules for testing of alarms and critical safety devices.
Breakdown maintenance and repairs.
Reports of repairs and maintenance of hull and machinery items.
Drawings and Instruction Manuals.

Protective and Preservative Maintenance Schedule
Steel structure and items of machinery and spare parts, which require protection against corrosive media, cargo and environment, shall be covered under such maintenance. De- scaling and painting of decks, tank tops, deck-equipment, hull external, all tanks including double bottom tanks, protection of pipelines, cleaning up of tanks and bilges, washing and painting of accommodation and machinery bulkheads shall be carried out so as to maintain the vessel in good condition.

Predictive Maintenance Schedule
The criteria for predictive maintenance schedules shall be based on the status and performance of various machinery and equipment as well as the classification requirements. The comparison of performance parameters vis-à-vis maker‘s recommended data or shop trial/sea trial data shall be used for evaluation of maintenance requirements.
While formulating the predictive maintenance schedules, following parameters shall also be included apart from other parameters stipulated in the respective maker‘s manuals for various equipment.
Running hours since installation/last overhaul
Bridge gauge readings, bearing clearances and crank shaft deflection (for engines)
Analysis of cooling water and lubricants.
Manufacturer‘s recommendations updated with shipboard experience.
Classification requirements. | Guidelines on Planned Maintenance

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
For ship‘s hull, decks and tanks, following factors shall form the criteria:
Existing maintenance standards and conditions
Availability of resources
Weather conditions
The time intervals and details in the cases of predictive maintenance shall be formulated on the basis of observation and experience and with the concurrence of the Superintendent.

Testing of Alarms & Safety Devices
Audio and visual alarms, cut-outs of equipment, wherever provided shall be tested/ checked at intervals, as detailed under section 7 — Ship Operations.
Alarm devices shall not be by-passed under normal operating conditions. However, if by- passing becomes necessary, all concerned shall be informed. This shall be followed by exhibiting visual signs and appropriate log entries. Watch keeping personnel shall exercise extra caution till the fault in alarm system is rectified. Superintendent shall be immediately advised to arrange requisite spares/shore assistance, if required, so as to restore alarms/automation to its normal working condition.

Record Keeping
Record of all planned maintenance or breakdown maintenance carried out on board shall be kept by the Chief Engineer Officer and Chief Officer for their respective departments along with outstanding planned maintenance tasks (if any). These records shall include details such as running hours, type of defect, maintenance carried out, spares consumed and other observations, if any, ships with computerised maintenance may not be required to maintain separate records, which may serve as a guideline for future maintenance.
A record of running defects, identified during voyage and defects noticed during periodic inspection of machinery and equipment shall also be maintained by Deck and Engine Departments. Such defects shall be monitored/periodically reviewed for timely rectification. Status of deferred repairs, if any, shall be readily available with the Chief Engineer Officer and Chief Officer. Status of running defects shall also be sent to respective Operating Divisions along with Planned Maintenance System.
The schedules and maintenance carried out during each month shall be entered in the Engine Abstract and Abstract of Mates Work.
Record of major overhaul, repairs and maintenance done by workshop or yard shall be maintained by the concerned departments.
Record of defects/failures of recurring nature of an equipment and corresponding remedial action shall also be available with the Chief Engineer Officer and Chief Officer.

Drawings and Instruction Manuals
A set of drawings and instruction manuals shall be kept on board and indexed as detailed under Section 11.
In case of any structural changes, modifications, renewal, retrofit or decommissioning of any equipment, the records shall be suitably amended (if applicable) with the concurrence of the concerned Superintendent. | For ship‘s hull, decks and tanks, following factors shall form the criteria:

Procedure for Classification Surveys
Superintendent, Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall carry out adequate planning and monitoring for compliance to applicable Class requirements and carry out surveys well before the due date. Accordingly, superintendent shall monitor status of surveys closely and advise vessels accordingly.
Master is responsible for maintaining on board all the statutory and classification certificates, as well as, certificates of various equipment of the vessel. Master, while taking over the command of the vessel shall ensure that all the certificates are in order and valid. Any deficiency shall be reported to the concerned Superintendent.
The Chief Engineer Officer is responsible for maintaining on board all the certificates related to the CSM/SSM cycle, machinery, as well as, certificates of various equipment. He shall ensure that all the certificates under his charge are in order and valid. Any deficiency shall be reported to the concerned Superintendent.
The Chief Officer shall be responsible for maintaining the Register for Lifting Appliances and Loose Gear and test certificates of cargo gear including wire ropes, cordage, mooring ropes and atmospheric gas sampling instruments.
The Radio Officer/person assigned such duty shall be responsible for maintaining the certificates related to radio equipment and navigational equipment, including Makers‘ certificates concerning the equipment. Any deficiency shall be reported to the concerned Superintendent.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the certificates are complete and include all items actually surveyed, as well as, items for which waiver has been granted by the Class. Any omissions in certificates due to oversight shall be immediately reported to the concerned Superintendent.
All surveys shall be planned and completed within the window period.
Master/Chief Engineer Officer shall inform the Superintendent/Agents regarding survey requirement and the readiness so that surveyor can be arranged at a specific port. They shall also send following information to the Superintendent at intervals specified below:
Certificate status – every three month.
Completion report – after survey.
Condition of Class imposed/deleted, if any, as soon as imposed/deleted.
The survey preparation shall be in accordance with the checklist and survey rules provided by the class.
Due courtesy shall be shown to the Surveyor and he shall be accompanied by the concerned officer to the equipment/area to be surveyed. As far as practicable, the Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall also accompany the surveyor.
After survey, surveyor may be requested to sign in relevant survey register/record on board.
Records of survey items credited shall be maintained on board. | Procedure for Classification Surveys

10.4	Procedure for Repairs
Endeavour shall be made by Master and Chief Engineer Officer to carry out repairs and maintenance of routine nature by utilising expertise, skill, equipment and material available on board.
In case shore workshop assistance is required, the superintendent shall be notified in advance by e-mail/other available means, prior arrival port. Depending on the nature of defect, additional information from the list referred below shall be furnished:
Location/port where repairs are to be undertaken
Type of machinery or equipment
Maker, Serial number and specifications
Nature of defect, Nature of repairs – temporary/permanent
Items required for rectification
Job to be done in situ or to be taken ashore
Spares held on board
Details of accessory work involved like staging, gas free certificate, removal/refitting of pipes, coolers, manholes etc.
Material and dimensions
Hot work involved, if any
Expected port stay
Is this defect covered under guarantee or insurance or third party damage
Is this item attended/repaired earlier? If so, date/part of repair/RS Number shall be mentioned.
Repair Specification shall be prepared through DANAOS System or as per the instructions provided in the front cover sheet of the RS memo book.
The allocation of the registered workshops at different ports shall be done by the regional office/agent in consultation with the superintendent at Head Office.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer, in consultation with the Company‘s regional office/ agents, shall ensure that the work scope approved by the superintendent is allocated to a workshop, which is empanelled by the Company and has an approved tariff. Workshops shall be normally allocated on rotation basis by the superintendent/agent. Deviations, if any, shall be done with the concurrence of the superintendent at the Head Office.
In normal course job shall be entrusted to the workshop only with prior sanction from superintendent. However, when port stay is limited and in instances where HO/ Superintendent is not contactable and workshop assistance is essential for safety and productivity of the vessel, the job may be given to workshop on emergency basis. After entrusting the job, the superintendent shall be informed promptly of the steps taken for expeditious repairs.
The repair specification with all details viz. material/dimensions etc. shall be handed over to the repairer and job explained at site to ensure that the work scope has been well understood.
Job progress shall be communicated to superintendent in the head office on daily basis.
On job completion, the respective system, equipment or machinery shall be tried out to ensure that the repairs carried out are satisfactory.
All corrections/deletions in the R.S., completion copies and work done certificates shall be initialled by concerned Officers.
Jobs which do not affect vessel's schedule or safety shall not be done in overtime hours. | 10.4	Procedure for Repairs

However, when port stay is limited and in instances where HO/ Superintendent is not contactable and workshop assistance is essential for safety and productivity of the vessel, the job may be given to workshop on emergency basis. After entrusting the job, the superintendent shall be informed promptly of the steps taken for expeditious repairs.
The repair specification with all details viz. material/dimensions etc. shall be handed over to the repairer and job explained at site to ensure that the work scope has been well understood.
Job progress shall be communicated to superintendent in the head office on daily basis.
On job completion, the respective system, equipment or machinery shall be tried out to ensure that the repairs carried out are satisfactory.
All corrections/deletions in the R.S., completion copies and work done certificates shall be initialled by concerned Officers.
Jobs which do not affect vessel's schedule or safety shall not be done in overtime hours.

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.4.1   Landing Items for Repairs
Items requiring lead-time for repairs ashore, which cannot be connected to the vessel in the same port, shall be landed with the concurrence of attending Superintendent. An immediate telex or fax shall be sent to the Superintendent with details of items landed ashore and of the party with whom items have been landed. A landing receipt shall be obtained from the workshop/agent and one set retained on board. | 10.4.1   Landing Items for Repairs

10.5	Procedures for Dry-dock Repair Specifications (DDRS)
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the dry-dock repair specifications are prepared approximately 3 months before due date. Master shall arrange to forward the consolidated dry dock specifications to the Operating Division.
The dry-dock RS shall be prepared on blank sheets and sent to concerned superintendent. Deck repair specifications shall include repairs of all bridge instruments and communication equipment as well as the automation equipment pertaining to safety items. Similarly, the engine repair specifications, apart from machinery repairs, shall include all electrical equipment repairs and automation equipment in the Engine Room and deck machinery.
All fresh repairs jobs, arising after inspection by surveyors/superintendents, shall be included in the repair format to enable attending superintendent obtain time-cost quotation from the yard.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall report to the attending superintendent for day- to-day instructions. They may delegate some of the operational duties to Chief Officer and Second Engineer Officer or any other officer. They are also responsible for maintaining all records for testing and ensuring that the jobs are carried out to their satisfaction under the guidance of superintendent.
The following details shall also be incorporated as required:
Spares required for the job and stock held on board.
Details of accessory work removal and refitting of insulation, panelling, pipes, coolers or floor plates etc. to carry out actual work.
Describe scope of cleaning work required before execution of the job.
Gas free/Man entry/Hot work permits, if required.
Items due for survey.
Any scaffolding/staging required (height of staging to be mentioned).
Requirement of Maker's representative or service technicians.
Whether job can be accomplished in-situ or parts need to be taken to shop.
Dry-dock job or the job, which can be completed afloat.

Docking
During the dry docking and lay up repairs Master shall continue to remain responsible for the safety of the vessel, all the officers and crew members. Chief Engineer Officer shall continue to be responsible for the safety of E/R, machinery spaces and other spaces under his specific charge.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the safe working practices are adopted by the yard and no hot work is undertaken unless the boundaries of the hot work location are identified.
The escape routes shall be clearly marked and explained to the yard‘s ship repair Manager. The ship/yard communication shall be established and understood for any emergency. VHF channel and telephone number of shore emergency stations like fire brigade, ambulance etc. shall be noted by all concerned and displayed on the notice board at the gangway, engine room and the control room.
All fresh repairs job arising after inspection by surveyors/superintendents shall be included in the repair format. | 10.5	Procedures for Dry-dock Repair Specifications (DDRS)

10.6	Spare Parts, Lubricants and Stores
Procedure for Preparation of Stores/Spares/Lubricants Indents and Supply
Instructions for processing stores/spares are given in the indent books. They shall be read carefully and strictly complied with.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the indents of stores/spares/lubricants are based on the projected operational requirement and the inventory figures of various items. The indents shall be forwarded to the superintendent on requirement, preferably on quarterly basis.
Stores
The requirement of stores and consumables for safe and efficient operation of the vessel shall be forwarded to the Technical Department of the respective Division by Master and Chief Engineer Officer on the Company‘s standard format. All relevant columns in the indent need to be filled up prior forwarding it to the respective operating divisions.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that the indents of stores/spares/lubricants are based on the projected operational requirement and the inventory figures of various items.
The Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall forward monthly return of stores received to the Technical Department. The Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall also intimate to the Technical Superintendent and Purchase Department the list of pending store items sanctioned but not supplied. Stores supplied to the ships are free of asbestos content.
LSA/FFA/SOPEP/ISPS Stores
All statutory and for safety of ship and personnel, stores items like LSA/FFA/SOPEP/ ISPS items, nautical publications and charts etc. have to be consolidated in separate indent/PR and not to be mixed with other misc. stores requirements. Relevant information as applicable for required item must be clearly specified to ensure correct/timely supply. Reasons for indenting (e.g. expiry date etc.) should be recorded in the remarks column. Proper planning to be done on board and indent raised timely (not after expiry of an item). Charts can only be exception for short notices. This procedure will help in close monitoring of timely and complete supply of all statutory requirements.
The above indent, in prescribed format shall be transmitted electronically to the Operating Division. The concerned Superintendent will sanction same and forward a hard copy to the Purchase Department of Head Office and the vessel.
Similarly, for medicines the existing Indent Form shall continue to be used, however, same may be forwarded to the Operating Division electronically. For vessels fitted with the DANAOS, requisition should be raised through DANAOS system.
All other store indents to be despatched as per existing procedures.
Procedure for Emergency Indents (Stores)
Consistent with the safety, operational demands and productivity of the vessel, any store item required shall be procured through emergency indent/PR on DANAOS. Proper justification is required for indenting through an emergency indent.
The Master and Chief Engineer Officer are advised to exercise due diligence in raising emergency indent. Any stores/spares which can affect safety/sailing of the vessel, to be raised in emergency indent.
The indent shall be made in the specific format and instructions given in the format shall be complied with. | 10.6	Spare Parts, Lubricants and Stores

Even if the request is made over fax/e-mail, a confirmatory copy of the indent referring to previous correspondence shall be despatched from the same port or next port.
On receipt of indents, superintendent shall scrutinise and sanction required quantities and intimate the vessel suitably.
On receipt of stores/lubricants on board, GR shall be done in DANAOS System.
Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall forward status of pending indents to the superintendent on monthly basis.
Spare Parts
Necessary spares for carrying out proper maintenance and compliance with Statutory Regulations, Class and the Company requirements shall be maintained on board. The control of spares consumption shall be done through ship‘s requisition and returns of spares received. Spare part inventory shall be maintained in DANAOS (wherever fitted) Module of Maintenance. Spares supplied to the ships are free of asbestos content.
The Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall forward to the Technical Superintendent their respective requirements of spares on six monthly basis on the Company‘s standard format or through DANAOS. While preparing their indents/PR, the Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall comply with the instructions described on the inside cover of the format or guidelines in the DANAOS. For prompt processing, it is imperative that indents are filled in diligently and checked prior dispatching them to H.O. required details including of machinery and equipment, specifications and address of the OEM (if applicable), must be included or commented suitably. All required columns in the indent i.e. ROB, Last Used, need to be filled up prior forwarding it to the respective operating divisions.
The Master and Chief Engineer Officer on receipt of spares shall check for correct supply and any discrepancy in quality, quantity or specifications shall be immediately brought to the notice (within 30 days from receipt of spares on board) of the Superintendent for taking corrective action. The Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall forward monthly return of spare parts received to the Technical Department of their Division promptly (Statement of Spares) for timely settling of the bills. Due credence, needs to be given to the future planning, anticipation of spares/stores/lub oils required in normal operation and at the time of dry- docking. Procurement through emergency indents shall be avoided, as far as possible.
In cases where the requirement of spares is urgent, the Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall indicate the requirements by phone followed by fax/phone/e-mail and later confirm the same by sending in the Company‘s standard format. Master and Chief Engineer Officer shall forward status of pending indents for spares to the superintendent on monthly basis.
Lubricants
The indent for different grades of lubricants required (considering the reserve lub oils indicated in 7.2.4) shall be made by the Chief Engineer Officer and sent to the Technical Superintendent on Company‘s standard format, where the lubricants are supplied by the Company. The Technical Superintendent shall review and sanction the requirements and forward the indent to the Purchase Department for supply. The Technical Superintendent shall follow up with the Purchase Department to ensure prompt and proper supply of all the required lubricants to the vessel. However, if the lubricants are supplied by the Operator, the requisition shall be forwarded to the Base Port. | Even if the request is made over fax/e-mail, a confirmatory copy of the indent referring to previous correspondence shall be despatched from the same port or next port.

10.7	Superintendent‘s Inspections
Superintendent‘s Inspection Report (SIR) is a very vital feedback and requires to be filled up factually, diligently and timely with due importance to all the key issues onboard the vessel. Checklist provided in Shipboard SMS Manual.
The frequency of superintendent‘s visit in out-port shall depend on vessel‘s requirements like dry-docking, survey, major maintenance schedules and breakdown repairs.
The Superintendent shall inspect the hull, cargo area, tanks (if required), decks, E.R. and other machinery spaces. He shall also inspect all the LSA & FFA equipment, emergency alarms and emergency cut-outs and all items as per Superintendent Inspection Report.
After inspection of the vessel, its equipment and the above enumerated records, the Superintendent‘s Inspection Report (SIR) shall be completed at least once in six months and submitted to the group incharge.
Master and chief engineer officer shall keep following papers ready, for handing over to the Superintendent prior to his disembarking.
All the Statutory and Class Certificates
Dispensation Validity, if applicable
All Register as per SMS
Safety Check-list files
Cargo Plans
Drug & Alcohol Records
Log Books
Oil Record Book
Bunker Procedure, Plans & Oil Pollution Contingency Plans and Record of SOPEP/ SMPEP Drills
Maintenance Record
Crews list
List of pending spares & stores
Indents, if any
Defects lists, if any
Status of Survey list
ROB - Bunkers & Lub Oil
Lubrication charts/schedule/tail shaft conditioning system and records
Any other specific document for which Head Office follow up action is required
SMS files such as
Shipboard Internal & External Audit records
Master‘s Verification & Review reports
Record of SHEC meeting minutes
Accident & Near Miss/Hazardous Occurrence reports
Record of Emergency Drills
FSI/GI/PSC reports
ISPS Internal & External Audit records
ISPS documents with respect to yearly reviews of SSA and SSP, drills and exercises, security incidents, contingencies, inspections of security equipments, security meetings, lighting and relevant issues.
All CSRs to be in sequence as issued by DGS/Flag Administration. | 10.7	Superintendent‘s Inspections

After inspection of the vessel, its equipment and the above enumerated records, the Superintendent‘s Inspection Report (SIR) shall be completed at least once in six months and submitted to the group incharge.
Master and chief engineer officer shall keep following papers ready, for handing over to the Superintendent prior to his disembarking.
All the Statutory and Class Certificates
Dispensation Validity, if applicable
All Register as per SMS
Safety Check-list files
Cargo Plans
Drug & Alcohol Records
Log Books
Oil Record Book
Bunker Procedure, Plans & Oil Pollution Contingency Plans and Record of SOPEP/ SMPEP Drills
Maintenance Record
Crews list
List of pending spares & stores
Indents, if any
Defects lists, if any
Status of Survey list
ROB - Bunkers & Lub Oil
Lubrication charts/schedule/tail shaft conditioning system and records
Any other specific document for which Head Office follow up action is required
SMS files such as
Shipboard Internal & External Audit records
Master‘s Verification & Review reports
Record of SHEC meeting minutes
Accident & Near Miss/Hazardous Occurrence reports
Record of Emergency Drills
FSI/GI/PSC reports
ISPS Internal & External Audit records
ISPS documents with respect to yearly reviews of SSA and SSP, drills and exercises, security incidents, contingencies, inspections of security equipments, security meetings, lighting and relevant issues.
All CSRs to be in sequence as issued by DGS/Flag Administration.

Extension of Superintendent Inspection Report
In exceptional circumstances when Superintendent Inspection could not be carried out within the stipulated period, extension may be considered by DPA in following cases:
Application from the department must specify the extension period.
The satisfactory inspection of the vessel either by PSC or FSI or Class (Last Report if done) or essentially joint inspection by Master and Chief Engineer Officer in line with SIR and submission of evidence of compliance.
Extension to Superintendent Inspection Report to be proposed by the operating division specifying the circumstances which were beyond their control along with the steps taken towards completing Superintendent Inspection Report within due period as per Company SMS Procedure Manual Section 10.4 – Performance monitoring.
Compliance with the requirement of Superintendent Inspection Report as detailed under Shipboard SMS Manual under respective section as mentioned above. | Extension of Superintendent Inspection Report

10.8	Hull and Superstructure Maintenance
Chief Officer shall be responsible for all maintenance of ship‘s hull, decks, accommodation, bulkheads, superstructure, mast houses, ballast tanks, deck pipelines and valves, deck and fittings, ladders and companion ways, cofferdams, deck store rooms, chain lockers, crane (if any) and any other areas under his charge.
Chief Engineer Officer shall be responsible for maintenance and upkeep of E.R. bulkheads, tank tops and various machinery platforms, cofferdams and storage tanks bulkheads and steering flat, crane machinery and other compartments, under his charge.

General Maintenance

Lubrication
Special attention shall be paid to lubrication schedules. Equipment and components requiring lubrication shall be lubricated at intervals stipulated in the instruction manuals.
All lubrication points shall be easily identifiable by the person carrying out lubrication. Grease nipples shall not be painted.
All open gears and pinions shall be cleaned and greased once in a month.
Shafts, on which sliding movements are required, such as engaging and disengaging of gear in winches and windlass, shall also be cleaned and greased once in a month to ensure proper operation.
All lubricating oil tanks, if used, shall be kept clean and filled with sufficient lubricating oil. Filters, if any, shall also be checked, cleaned or replaced as, necessary.

Following shall be stencilled or conspicuously marked on each tank:


TANK NO:	GRADE	CAPACITY IN LTS


Sufficient stock of lubricants shall be maintained on board the ship for an intended voyage.
A lubrication card/schedule shall be maintained for all the machinery/equipment, which requires lubrication. The Chief Officer shall be responsible for lubrication schedule of all the equipment under his charge. The 2nd Engineer Officer, in consultation with the Chief Engineer Officer, shall prepare the lubrication schedule for machinery items. The Master and the Chief Engineer Officer shall ensure that all the lubricating points are covered under above schedule and the schedules are strictly followed.

Maintenance in General
A planned maintenance scheme shall be undertaken by the Chief Officer, in consultation with the Master, so that all exposed deck areas, touch up on hull, superstructure, cranes etc. are attended in a systematic logical and phased manner. This continuity shall be maintained by the officers joining the vessel.
Any deviations from the maintenance schedule due to unforeseen factors like accidental damage, adverse weather conditions, restrictions imposed by port authorities etc. may | 10.8	Hull and Superstructure Maintenance

Maintenance in General
A planned maintenance scheme shall be undertaken by the Chief Officer, in consultation with the Master, so that all exposed deck areas, touch up on hull, superstructure, cranes etc. are attended in a systematic logical and phased manner. This continuity shall be maintained by the officers joining the vessel.
Any deviations from the maintenance schedule due to unforeseen factors like accidental damage, adverse weather conditions, restrictions imposed by port authorities etc. may

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
delay the completion; but the sequential continuity of planned maintenance shall be maintained.

Application of Paints
When a painting is undertaken, the vessel‘s painting scheme/system and the paint manufacturer‘s instructions shall be carefully followed with regard to surface preparation, use of primers, thinners, coating intervals and compatibility with other paints. Consideration shall be given to the expected weather conditions and for the time required to complete the final coat.
Surface preparation of the steel structure prior application of the paint is of paramount importance.
Proper use of power tools shall be made to prepare the surface as best as possible.
In absence of power tools manual chipping, de-scaling shall be carried out.
Necessary precautions for personal safety, ventilation, electrical shocks, fire and explosion safety shall be taken while using power tools and while painting.
Although painting of the ship hull is undertaken in the dry-dock, touch up of the mechanical and abrasive damage areas shall be done by ship‘s crew at a suitable port/anchorage stay.
Restrictions, if any, by the local port authorities towards painting of vessel‘s hull in port shall be checked through agents/branch offices prior commencement of work.
Adequate precautions shall be taken so that no paint spills on the deck or over side.
Necessary precautions for lighting, ventilation and continuous monitoring of atmosphere shall be taken while painting in enclosed spaces.
After descaling and on completion of surface preparation, the area shall be immediately painted with a primer coat.
In order to protect the surface from the exposure to atmosphere for long time after requisite primer and under coats, a coat of finishing paint shall be applied immediately.
Refer section 7.10.13 for safety while painting.

Ship‘s Hull
Hull maintenance shall include maintenance of main deck, superstructure, crane structure, mast houses etc. All possible efforts shall be made to carry out maintenance at anchorage, alongside or at sea depending upon the weather conditions, adhering to vessel‘s painting scheme.
While painting of the hull is normally undertaken during lay up/dry dock and touch up is done as and when required, the maintenance of decks, superstructure, crew accommodation, mast houses, cranes, deck machinery, ventilators and other fixtures shall be done during the voyage in a phased manner, as per the planned maintenance schedule.

Main Deck & Superstructure
Special attention shall be paid to the main deck, forecastle deck and poop decks.
The foundation of mooring winches, windlass, towing winch, tugger winch and other deck machinery shall be specially examined and chipped/painted as per painting schedule.
All vents/exhausts shall be examined every three months. | delay the completion; but the sequential continuity of planned maintenance shall be maintained.

Masts/Radar Post/Christmas Tree
The securing arrangements of the navigation lights, and wireless antennae shall be checked at least once in three months and greased, as necessary.
A visual inspection for cracks of the base of masts/mast table shall be done every three months.

Ballast Tanks
All ballast tanks shall be opened, well ventilated, cleaned thoroughly and inspected annually. The condition of tank internals viz. solid floors, top and bottom longitudinal, brackets, gussets and other structural parts shall be examined for any wastage, damage, deformation or buckling. The pipes passing through the Ballast tanks shall be examined for any wastage, loose clamps and signs of corrosion.
Ventilation shall be kept on during the tank inspection and if more than one manhole is provided in the tank, all the manholes shall be kept open.
The lighting used during the tank inspection shall be maintained in good condition and acceptable as per rules/Industry guidelines.
The tank coating shall be specifically examined.
Hull plating below the suction of bell mouth and striker plate below the sounding pipes shall be specially examined for any wastage due to the corrosion.
The pipelines passing through the tanks shall be carefully examined for any signs of corrosion. Securing clamps for pipes shall also be examined and repaired/replaced if found damaged or corroded.
Tank manholes, air vents and sounding pipes shall be carefully examined. Particular attention shall be paid to deck penetration.

Fresh Water Tanks
Fresh water tanks shall be inspected once in every dry dock and cleaned.
The tank coating, if required, to be restored shall be done by approved fresh water tank coating, which is lead free.
Tank interior shall be washed with fresh water and made dry prior filling the tank for human consumption.

Engine Room & Machinery Spaces
Engine room/machinery spaces shall be kept clean, free of rust, oil and oily residues at all times. Engine room bilges shall be kept dry and leakages, if any, shall be attended promptly. The spaces shall be given a coat of paint as and when required.
All drip trays shall be kept dry and clean at all times.
Sea chests, overboard discharges, stub pieces to shipside openings, storm valves and ER frames shall be specially examined for any wastage or corrosion.
Sea chests shall be blown through, as required.

Machinery & Equipment
Machinery and equipment shall be degreased and soap washed as required. All machinery shall be normally painted every 5 years. However, depending on the condition, the same may be deferred, if required. | Masts/Radar Post/Christmas Tree

Other Spaces
Chain locker shall be sounded daily and records maintained. The pumping out arrangement shall be checked at least once every three months. Thorough inspections and maintenance shall be carried out during the planned lay-ups/dry-dock.
The paint locker shall be maintained in a clean condition. Paint drums shall be stowed and secured properly and lids shall be properly closed to avoid flammable vapours. Chief Officer shall thoroughly inspect paint locker at least once in a month. Fixed fire fighting system for paint lockers shall be blown through at least once in six months.

Means of Embarkation and Disembarkation
Means of embarkation and disembarkation shall be inspected every month to ensure that they are in suitable condition for the intended purposes taking into account any restriction related to safe loading. Means of embarkation and disembarkation include MOT ladder, accommodation ladders, pilot ladders, rescue boat embarkation ladders etc.
Periodic inspection and maintenance of ladders shall include the following:
Check for distortion and cracks
Check for corrosion, particularly where aluminium ladders have mild steel fittings
Bent stanchions shall be replaced; side ropes shall be inspected and replaced, if required
Underside of the ladder shall also be inspected for condition, distortion, cracks and corrosion
Safety nets shall be checked for wear, damage, impregnation of grease & chemicals. Records of inspection and maintenance shall cover date of inspection/maintenance, maintenance work undertaken and names of persons/workshop undertaking such maintenance and due date for next inspection.

Load Line Items
All items related to load line inspection shall be checked, as per the format of the Classification Society (e.g. Conditions of Freeboard Assignment of Load Line).

Windlass/Winches
Brake lining of windlass and mooring winches shall be checked monthly.
The markings on joining shackles shall be kept painted and well marked.
For easy identification, marking of the cables shall be done by seizing wire and canvas.
Prior commencement of sea passage, both anchors shall be properly housed, lashed and brakes fully tightened.
Spurling pipes shall be covered and cemented prior long sea passage.
It shall be ensured that brake band stoppers, located at the bottom, are in place and the clearances are duly adjusted.
Communication System
Communication system shall be checked between Bridge/Engine Room/Steering Flat prior sailing from or arriving any port.

Booby hatch
Booby hatch entrance door rubber retaining channel, rubber packing as well as the coamings shall be examined every 6 months. | Other Spaces

LSA/FFA Equipment
Refer SOLAS Chapter III, for instructions on maintenance. The following paragraphs indicate instructions and maintenance procedures for various LSA/FFA equipment. The list given below is not exhaustive. It is possible that some equipment listed below is not fitted on ships. It is also possible that the ship is fitted with certain equipment, which is not listed in this section. For precise instructions on maintenance practices, the manufacturer‘s manuals shall be referred.

Safety Operational Booklets
The fire safety operational booklet shall contain the necessary information and instruction for the safe operation of the ship and cargo handling operations in relation to fire safety. The booklet shall include information concerning the crew‘s responsibilities for the general fire safety of the ship while loading and discharging cargo Code, as appropriate. (SOLAS II- 2/16.2.1)
The fire Safety Operational Booklet shall also include provisions for preventing fire spread to the cargo area due to ignition of flammable vapours and include procedures for cargo tank gas- purging and/or gas-freeing (SOLAS II-2/16.3.1). The Fire Safety Operational Booklet shall be provided in each crew mess room and recreation room, or in each crew cabin. (SOLAS II-2/16.2.2).The booklet shall be written in the working language of the ship. (SOLAS II-2/16.2.3).The booklet may be combined with the Fire Training Manual (SOLAS II-2/16.2.4).

Rescue Boat/Lifeboat
The Administration has granted dispensation on offshore supply vessels for carrying one rescue boat operated with outboard engine in place of lifeboat due to space constraint. The rescue boat is operated through a motor driven single arm davit. Additional life rafts have been placed on board, as per Administration recommendations.
Particulars of each rescue boat/lifeboat shall contain Type, Boat Size, Weight of empty boat with equipment, Weight of fully laden boat, Number of persons, Hoisting Load, Hoisting Speed, Lowering Speed and Wire Rope (size and construction).

Weekly
The general emergency alarm shall be tested.
All rescue boats shall be moved from their stowed position to the extent necessary to demonstrate satisfactory operation of the launching appliances. This shall be done without any persons on board the boat subject to conducive weather/sea conditions. Details of mandatory weekly inspections of rescue boats shall be entered in the logbook.
Check the fuel quantity in the outboard motor (OBM) and try out OBM.
Emergency lights (if provided) are working.
Skates in position and securing straps of them in good condition.
Check that toggle painter is rigged and secured.
Check that oars, boathooks and loose gear are in good condition. | LSA/FFA Equipment

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Monthly
In addition to the weekly inspection routines, following shall be carried out:
As far as is reasonable and practicable, rescue boat shall be launched and manoeuvred in the water with its assigned operating crew every month during an abandon ship drill (SOLAS Ch. III, Reg. 19, Para 3.3.6). Records shall be maintained. However, due to the operational constraints, if same cannot be achieved, same shall be recorded with reasons thereof.
All rescue boats/lifeboats shall be turned out monthly from their stowed position. This shall be done without any persons on board the boat subject to conducive weather/sea conditions. Records shall be maintained.
Check that updated muster list is prominently displayed on all the accommodation decks
Davit and winch shall be lubricated (Diagram of lubrication points with recommended lubricants shall be available).
No air bubbles in the boat compass.
Check the inventory as per the inventory list.
Check that rescue boat/lifeboat pyrotechnics are in place, valid and in good condition.
Drain plug in place.
Retro reflective tape is in place.
Check that bilges are clean and dry.
Check that a list of replaceable parts and spare parts, with the list of sources of such spare parts are available.
Check that boat hoisting handle is in place and in satisfactory condition.
Check that boat lowering lever located on the boat deck is operating freely. Grease, if necessary.
Check the condition of the boarding ladder and its securing arrangement on the deck.
Check that following warning sign are prominently displayed near the boat winch and also at the electrical control panel.
CAUTION
Ensure that electric power supply is switched off from the control panel prior to engaging the handle to hoisting winch.
Ensure that manual handle is disengaged from boat hoisting winch before switching on the electric power.

Quarterly
In addition to the monthly inspection routines, following shall be carried out:
In case rescue boat cannot be launched once a month due to operational constraints as stated in monthly routine above, same shall be launched and manoeuvred in the water with its assigned operating crew once every three months. Records shall be maintained.
Check that electrical hoisting switch and the emergency stop switch are working perfectly before launching.
Check that power supply to the push button switch box is disconnected before the davit cradle reaches the contact surface. Effectiveness of the limit switch shall be checked. | Monthly

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Half-yearly
In addition to the quarterly inspection routines, following shall be carried out:
Boat falls to be coated with WRP.
Rust spots on the davit arrangement are chipped, cleaned, primered and painted.
See that all movable parts move smoothly, lubricate if necessary and also
before each boat drill
after weather conditions resulting in heavy spray.
after paint work on davit arrangement.
Examine welding connections in davit arrangement to ensure that no cracks have formed. Take special care with foundation and supports for davit, winch, brackets for wire sheaves, attachment for lugs and fittings and parts of davits not visible with boats in stowed position.
Check lubricating oil level for the winch.
Check condition of toggle painter, sea anchor, oil bag and tripping line.
Boat launching instruction and warning sign are legible and illuminated by emergency source.
Annual
In addition to the half-yearly inspection routines, following shall be carried out:
Rescue boat/lifeboat and launching appliances are subject to a thorough examination annually. After the thorough exam, dynamic winch brake test (without compliments) shall be carried out by maker‘s authorised personnel or DGS approved service centre.
Whenever manufacturer‘s certified facilities/DGS approved service centre are not available, other reputed manufacturer‘s service personnel may be utilised subject to the servicing is done in presence of a Class.
Charge the fire extinguishers.
Five Yearly
In addition to the annual inspection routines, following shall be carried out:
Rescue boat/lifeboat and launching appliances are subject to a thorough examination. After the thorough exam, dynamic winch brake test (with 110% weight of fully laden rescue boat/lifeboat) shall be carried out by maker‘s authorised personnel or DGS approved service centre in the presence of Class.
Whenever manufacturer‘s certified facilities/DGS approved service centre are not available, other reputed manufacturer‘s service personnel may be utilised subject to the servicing is done in presence of a Class.
Rescue Boat/Lifeboat Falls
Rescue boat/lifeboat falls are to be approved by Administration. Whenever Administration approved rescue boat/lifeboat falls are not available, rescue boat/lifeboat falls duly tested, approved and certified by one of the IACS members, can be used and the Company shall be informed to obtain permission from DGS to use the Class approved wire falls in place of Administration approved rescue boat/lifeboat wire falls.
The life of a rescue boat/lifeboat fall is considered five years. The falls shall be inspected periodically with special regard to areas passing through sheaves and renewed, when necessary, due to deterioration of the falls or at least every five years, whichever is earlier. | Half-yearly

Life Rafts Weekly
Check that the life raft container is marked with markings viz. name of the vessel, maker‘s name or trade mark, serial number, name of approving authority, number of persons it is permitted to carry, SOLAS, type of emergency pack enclosed, date when last serviced, length of painter, maximum permitted height of stowage above waterline and launching instructions.
Check HRU connection and the lashing arrangement
Check that painter is connected to the weak link of the HRU
Check that the emergency light on the ship side near the fwd. life raft is working
Check that railing doors and the chains near the life rafts are not frozen. Grease if necessary.
Monthly
Carry out following in addition to the weekly routine:
Clean with fresh water
Try out the Hydrostatic release unit (if applicable)
Greasing of senhouse slip
Annually
Servicing of life raft ashore
Servicing of Hydrostatic release units (if applicable)
Life Jackets Fortnightly
Check the general condition of life jackets and ensure cleanliness.
Check that life jacket light and whistle are functional.
During the drills make sure that everyone has donned the lifejacket correctly.
Check that retro-reflective tape is pasted on each lifejacket.
Ensure ship‘s name and port of registry are clearly marked on all the life jackets.
Monthly
Check that additional lifejackets if provided on the vessel.
Check that sufficient number of child lifejackets are provided (as per SOLAS Chap. III).
10.9.4	Life Buoys
Number and disposition of life buoys to be as per the approved LSA plan.
Weekly
Check that S.I. Lights are working.
Check that all lifebuoys are properly bracketed in their respective places.
Check that lifelines are secured in such a way that they can be opened out easily.
Check that all S.I. Lights are attached to the buoys.
Monthly
In addition to the weekly routine carry out the following:
Change the retro-reflective tapes if smeared with dirt | Life Rafts Weekly

Paint the lifebuoys and stencil the ship‘s name and port of registry.
Change the retro-reflective tape.
10.9.5	Ship‘s Pyrotechnics
Parachute rockets – 12 Nos.
Line throwing apparatus and rockets – 4 Nos.
Check that the pyrotechnics are stowed in the bridge in clearly marked containers, away from electrical installations.
Lifeboat pyrotechnics shall be stored inside water-tight container in the respective lifeboats. Records of all pyrotechnics shall be maintained, details of which shall include the following:
Name of the supplier
Make and Expiry date
Copy of import invoice that shall bear the details of the product
Copy of Letter of Acceptance issued by the Directorate to the importers/distributors (if supplied in India)
Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) Monthly Checks
Test the beacon as per Maker‘s test procedures.
Check that the antenna and brackets are properly secured.
Perform self test and maintain records
Yearly Checks
EPIRBs onboard on ships shall undergo an Annual Performance Test in compliance with SOLAS Ch. IV Reg. 15. This test shall be carried out by SRC anniversary date (+/- 3 months) The test may be carried out onboard or ashore by an approved Service Centre.
Operational test shall be carried out with electronic test equipment with the assistance of shore-based workshop. However, the EPIRB shall be tested by an approved service centre during battery replacement or if any deficiency is observed during the course of inspection on board the ship.
Five Yearly Checks
Shore-based maintenance shall be carried out in accordance with requirements of SOLAS Ch.
IV Reg. 15 (MSC/Circ.1039) at an interval not exceeding five years or when battery replacement is due. Shore-based maintenance reports shall be maintained on board and a | Check that ship‘s name and port of registry are clearly legible on both sides of the buoy.

Check that there is no crack on the body

Lifeboat pyrotechnics shall be stored inside water-tight container in the respective lifeboats. Records of all pyrotechnics shall be maintained, details of which shall include the following:
Name of the supplier
Make and Expiry date
Copy of import invoice that shall bear the details of the product
Copy of Letter of Acceptance issued by the Directorate to the importers/distributors (if supplied in India)
Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) Monthly Checks
Test the beacon as per Maker‘s test procedures.
Check that the antenna and brackets are properly secured.
Perform self test and maintain records
Yearly Checks
EPIRBs onboard on ships shall undergo an Annual Performance Test in compliance with SOLAS Ch. IV Reg. 15. This test shall be carried out by SRC anniversary date (+/- 3 months) The test may be carried out onboard or ashore by an approved Service Centre.
Operational test shall be carried out with electronic test equipment with the assistance of shore-based workshop. However, the EPIRB shall be tested by an approved service centre during battery replacement or if any deficiency is observed during the course of inspection on board the ship.
Five Yearly Checks
Shore-based maintenance shall be carried out in accordance with requirements of SOLAS Ch.
IV Reg. 15 (MSC/Circ.1039) at an interval not exceeding five years or when battery replacement is due. Shore-based maintenance reports shall be maintained on board and a

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
label affixed to the exterior of the beacon indicating SBM provider and due date for next SBM. The SBM provider may affix a tamper proof seal or similar device on completion of the SBM. The maintenance interval may be aligned with the replacement date of the battery but not exceeding five years.
Whenever, false alert (EPIRB) is activated accidentally without the knowledge of shipboard personnel, the vessel is informed by MRCC/operating division on receiving the alert. Such false alerts shall be reset and the status shall be communicated in writing to MRCC/DG COMCENTRE and the operating division for cancellation of the alerts. The procedure is enumerated in ALRS Vol. V.
Search & Rescue Transponder (SART) Monthly Checks
Test the transponder as per maker‘s test procedures and record observations.
Check that mounting bracket is properly secured in place.
Check that buoyant line is attached to the transponder.
Yearly Checks
The SART may be tested on board the ship for its physical parameters and its signal strength by the inspecting authority at least once in a year. However, the SART shall be tested at an approved workshop during the replacement of the battery or if any deficiency is observed during the course of inspection on board the ship.
The vessel shall maintain initial service record. A record of annual testing of the equipment shall be maintained on board.
Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) – where applicable
Checks and maintenance of Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) shall be carried out as per maker‘s instructions.
Whenever, false alert (SSAS) is activated accidentally without the knowledge of shipboard personnel, the vessel is informed by MRCC/operating division on receiving the alert. Such false alerts shall be reset and the status shall be communicated in writing to MRCC/DG COMCENTRE and the operating division for cancellation of the alerts. The procedure is enumerated in ALRS Vol. V.
Disposal of discarded/obsolete LSA/FFA items
All expired, failed or condemned LSA and FFA shall be clearly marked/stenciled and stored in a safe isolated/designated place on board and landed ashore at the earliest opportunity to avoid misuse in a real emergency.
The recommended alternative is to identify authorized party/supplier and hand over the items or disposal in drydock/shipyard. On ONGC owned vessels, ONGC shall arrange safe disposal/removal when vessel arrives in base port.
Record of such items shall be maintained in LSA/FFA register including mention of storage location.
A receipt shall be obtained stating that the discarded items have been collected from the ship for safe disposal ashore. | label affixed to the exterior of the beacon indicating SBM provider and due date for next SBM. Fire Fighting Equipment Maintenance Instructions
The periodical maintenance and inspection routines of all fire protection, detection and extinction systems and appliances onboard shall be carried out in accordance with the ship's maintenance plan which should include the minimum elements of the IMO MSC.1/Circ.1432 on ―Revised guidelines for the maintenance and inspection of Fire Protection Systems and Appliances‖, as applicable.
The maintenance plan shall include at least the following fire protection systems and fire fighting system and appliances where installed:
Fire mains, fire pumps and hydrants, hoses, nozzles and international shore connections:
Fixed fire detection and fire alarm systems;
Fixed fire extinguishing systems and other extinguishing appliances;
Hyper Mist, fire detection and fire alarm systems;
Ventilations systems, including fire and smoke dampers, fans and their controls;
Emergency shutdown of fuel supply;
Fire doors, including their controls;
General Emergency Alarm system;
Emergency Escape Breathing devices;
Portable fire extinguisher, including spare charges;
Fire fighter‘s-outfits, Safety equipments with suits & Protective equipment suits;
Flammable gas detectors (SOLAS II-2/14.2.2.3 and 14.4).
The maintenance programme may be computer based. (SOLAS II-2/14.2.2.4)
Operational readiness:
All fire protection system and appliances should be, at all times, in good order and available for immediate use while the ship is in service. If a fire protection system is under repair, then suitable arrangements acceptable to the Recognized Organization that issued the pertinent Safety Certificate, shall be made to ensure safety is not diminished.
In cases where the Recognized Organization which has issued the vessel‟s Statutory Certificate determines that the equipment does not comply with the requirements of the corresponding mandatory regulations, they must approach the Directorate for an authorization for the issuance of the relevant Conditional Statutory Certificate prior to permit the vessel to operate. Any vessel in a port or dry-dock or anchorage or temporarily immobilized due to some reason, shall be construed to be as a vessel under operation.
10.9.6	Fire Mains, Hoses, Hydrants, and Nozzles
Following checks shall be done:
Monthly
Fire hoses shall be drained, dried up, coiled and stowed in the shade after use to prevent them from becoming brittle.
Verify all fire hydrants, hose and nozzles are in place, properly arranged and are in serviceable condition (Couplings and rubber washers are in good condition, hydrants and nozzles shall be lubricated, outside surface shall be polished and free of salt deposits).
Fire hose boxes shall be kept well maintained. | Fire Fighting Equipment Maintenance Instructions

Quarterly
Verify international shore connection(s) is in serviceable condition if fitted.

Annual
Visually inspect all accessible components for proper condition
Fire hoses shall be hydrostatically pressure tested up to working pressure.
Test all hydrant valves for proper operation and no leakage.
All fire nozzles are of correct size/type and maintained and working.
Relief valve on fire line shall be overhauled annually. Verify the setting of relief valve pressure once in a year.


10.9.7   Portable and Semi-portable Fire Extinguishers
A portable extinguisher is one, which is designed to be carried and operated by hand, and which in working order has a total weight of not more than 23 kg. A semi-portable fire extinguisher means wheeled (mobile) fire extinguishers of higher capacity.
The periodical inspection and maintenance of all the portable and semi-portable extinguishers onboard shall be governed, as a minimum, by the IMO Resolution A.951(23) - ―Improved guidelines for marine portable fire extinguishers.‖

Following shall be complied with as per DGS Engineering Circular No.06 dated 19.08.2013:

Monthly
All extinguishers shall be subject to a visual external check.
All extinguishers shall be stowed in their respective positions with the plunger caps/pins in place to prevent accidental release.
The date of filling and the date on which the extinguisher has been tested shall be clearly stenciled on the cylinder.

Annual
All fire extinguishers must be checked for proper location, charging pressure, and condition, according to the ship's Fire Control Plan (FCP) and should be subject to periodical inspections in accordance with the manufacturer‘s instructions and serviced at intervals not exceeding one year and duly recorded by a management level officer whose identity is clearly decipherable. During these services any plastic collars, etc. which may conceal the condition of the cylinder underneath need to be removed to aid in the inspection.
This servicing can be undertaken by ship-staff and should be carried out as part of a Planned Maintenance System with all necessary procedures, work instructions, tools and equipment readily available.
Each extinguisher should be provided with a sign (maintenance label) clearly and indelibly indicating that it has been examined on a certain date by a competent person.
Records of inspections should be maintained onboard for verification, showing, inter-alia, the date of inspection, the type of maintenance carried out. | Quarterly
Verify international shore connection(s) is in serviceable condition if fitted.

Annual
Visually inspect all accessible components for proper condition
Fire hoses shall be hydrostatically pressure tested up to working pressure.
Test all hydrant valves for proper operation and no leakage.
All fire nozzles are of correct size/type and maintained and working.
Relief valve on fire line shall be overhauled annually. Verify the setting of relief valve pressure once in a year.

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments |  |  | 
Charges of dry chemical/water type fire extinguishers should be renewed if, on checking, there is any indication of deterioration in the contents or as specified by the manufacturer, but in any case not later than once every five years.
The premixed agent in liquid charge-type AFFF (aqueous film-forming foam) and FFFP (film-forming fluoro-protein foam) fire extinguishers shall be replaced at least once every year. The agent in solid charge-type AFFF fire extinguishers shall be replaced once every 5 years.
Carbon dioxide extinguishers and gas expellant cartridges should be recharged or renewed if the gas loss by weight exceeds 10% of the original charge.
Dry powder extinguishers may suffer from compaction when subject to vibration. At least one extinguisher should therefore be discharged annually at random and the retention of contents checked. When the retention is found to be in excess of 15% of the initial charge, further extinguishers should be discharged to determine the average compaction that is seen to be occurring.
Any extinguisher or bottle which indicates excessive corrosion shall be replaced.
Five Year Service
At least one extinguisher of each type manufactured in the same year and kept onboard a ship should be test discharged once every five year intervals (as part of a fire drill), in any case.
Spare Charges, Additional Fire Extinguishers and Refilling of Extinguishers
Spare charges shall be provided for 100% of the first 10 extinguishers and 50% of the remaining fire extinguishers capable of being recharged onboard.
Not more than 60% total spare charges are required to be maintained onboard.
Instructions for recharging shall be carried on board.
For fire extinguishers which cannot be recharged onboard, additional ready-to-use portable fire extinguishers of the same quantity, type, capacity shall be carried in lieu of spare charges.
Periodic refilling of the cylinders should be in accordance with the manufacturer‘s recommendations. Only refills approved for the concerned extinguisher may be used for recharging.
Partially emptied extinguishers should be recharged immediately.

Maintenance chart: | Charges of dry chemical/water type fire extinguishers should be renewed if, on checking, there is any indication of deterioration in the contents or as specified by the manufacturer, but in any case not later than once every five years.
The premixed agent in liquid charge-type AFFF (aqueous film-forming foam) and FFFP (film-forming fluoro-protein foam) fire extinguishers shall be replaced at least once every year. The agent in solid charge-type AFFF fire extinguishers shall be replaced once every 5 years.
Carbon dioxide extinguishers and gas expellant cartridges should be recharged or renewed if the gas loss by weight exceeds 10% of the original charge.
Dry powder extinguishers may suffer from compaction when subject to vibration. At least one extinguisher should therefore be discharged annually at random and the retention of contents checked. When the retention is found to be in excess of 15% of the initial charge, further extinguishers should be discharged to determine the average compaction that is seen to be occurring.
Any extinguisher or bottle which indicates excessive corrosion shall be replaced.
Five Year Service
At least one extinguisher of each type manufactured in the same year and kept onboard a ship should be test discharged once every five year intervals (as part of a fire drill), in any case.
Spare Charges, Additional Fire Extinguishers and Refilling of Extinguishers
Spare charges shall be provided for 100% of the first 10 extinguishers and 50% of the remaining fire extinguishers capable of being recharged onboard.
Not more than 60% total spare charges are required to be maintained onboard.
Instructions for recharging shall be carried on board.
For fire extinguishers which cannot be recharged onboard, additional ready-to-use portable fire extinguishers of the same quantity, type, capacity shall be carried in lieu of spare charges.
Periodic refilling of the cylinders should be in accordance with the manufacturer‘s recommendations. Only refills approved for the concerned extinguisher may be used for recharging.
Partially emptied extinguishers should be recharged immediately.

Hydrostatic Pressure Testing
All portable and semi-portable fire extinguishers shall be hydrostatically pressure tested as per SMS Section 10.9.19.

10.9.8	Self Contained Breathing Apparatus and Fireman‘s Outfit
Only positive pressure type sets are recommended for use in enclosed spaces because, as their name implies, these maintain a positive pressure within the face mask at all times.
When using the equipment, the following should be noted:
The pressure gauge must be checked and monitored before and during use which indicates the pressure of the air remaining in the cylinder.
The operation of the audible low pressure alarm should be tested before use.
The signal code tag shall be attached to the life line.
Ample time should be allowed for getting out of the hazardous atmosphere. In any event, the user must exit immediately if the low pressure alarm sounds.
If the users suspect at any time that the equipment may not be operating satisfactorily, they should exit the space immediately.

Weekly Maintenance
Examine all breathing apparatus cylinder gauges to confirm they are in the correct pressure range

Monthly Maintenance
Verify lockers providing storage of the units containing their full inventory and equipment is in serviceable condition. Following checks shall include:
gas tightness of the mask,
cleanliness of visor,
elasticity of mask bands,
leakages in hoses and attachments (e.g. lifeline)
torch,
helmet,
fireman‘s axe and the protective clothing.
The air pressure of SCBA bottle and the whistle.
In event of drop in cylinder pressure, the same shall be charged up to full capacity at the earliest opportunity.

Annual Maintenance
Analysis of SCBA compressor output air to be done to check fitness for use including oil mist by approved agency and records shall be maintained (if fitted).
Check all breathing apparatus face masks and air demand valves are in serviceable condition

Five Year Service (Hydrostatic Pressure Testing)
All SCBA cylinders shall be hydrostatically pressure tested and records to be maintained as per SMS Section 10.9.19. | Hydrostatic Pressure Testing

10.9.9   Emergency Escape Breathing Device (EEBD)
This is compressed air or oxygen breathing device used for escape from a compartment where the atmosphere has become hazardous while a person is within it. It is primarily for use in accordance with the SOLAS requirements for escape from machinery or accommodation spaces in the event of a fire. Additional sets should be provided for use as emergency escape equipment during enclosed space entry.
EEBDs are for emergency escape, and should not be used as the primary means for entering oxygen deficient compartments, or while fighting fires.
The number and location of all EEBDs on board shall be as per the approved Fire Control Plan.
A general examination of EEBDs including cylinder pressure gauge has to carry out weekly to confirm they are in the correct pressure range.
Manufacturer‘s manual shall be followed for time-based routines, EEBD should be tested to ensure that it functions correctly. This test can be performed by operating the EEBD, as if it is being used, and checking the time the autohatch/safety valve remains closed. This should be as per the duration of the EEBD.
Five Year Service (Hydrostatic Pressure Testing)
Hydrostatic test for all EEBD cylinders and records shall be maintained in compliance with DGS Engine Circular No. 06 of 2013 dated 19.08.2013 Refer SMS Section 10.9.19.
Storage
When equipment is stored in wall cabinets, ensure visibility of cylinder contents gauge – daily check.
Fully extend shoulder strap and also the waist belt if fitted.
Store equipment ―ready for use‖ in cool dry environment, free from dust and dirt. Protect rubber part from direct sunlight.
International Shore Coupling (ISC)
Gasket/nut-bolts and washers shall be placed along with the coupling in the box clearly marked and placed on the bridge. Gasket shall be checked every month against becoming brittle. Two numbers open ended spanners for above nut-bolts shall be placed along with the unit.
Halon Fixed Installation System (where applicable)
Instructions provided by the manufacturers shall be strictly followed. 5/10/15 yearly routines of the Halon system including the pipelines are to be carried out as per Administration‘s requirements (ref. ENG Circular 06 dated 19.08.2013available on board).
Chief Engineer Officer shall be responsible for the maintenance of the system and shall take all precautions during testing and maintenance operations.
Pressure of Halon bottles to be recorded daily.
Pilot bottle pressure shall be checked once a week.
A general inspection of the system shall be carried out every week.
Halon release alarm shall be checked once a week.
Halon bottle and pilot bottle low pressure alarm shall be checked once a week. | 10.9.9   Emergency Escape Breathing Device (EEBD)
