Maintenance Guidelines
The periodical inspection and maintenance of Fixed CO2 Fire Extinguishing systems shall be broadly guided by the IMO Circular MSC.1/Circ.1432- ―Revised guidelines for the maintenance and inspection of fire protection systems and appliances and the IMO Circular MSC.1/Circ.1318, ―Guidelines for the maintenance and inspections of fixed carbon dioxide fire-extinguishing systems‖.
Weekly Inspection and Maintenance
A general inspection of the system The trial of ventilation/exhaust fan for CO2 Room.
Monthly Inspection and Maintenance
Trial of CO2 alarm.
Checking of Mechanical isolating valve.
All releasing controls are in the proper position and readily accessible for immediate use.
All discharge piping and pneumatic tubing is intact and has not been damaged.
All high pressure cylinders are in place and properly secured.
The manual release handles shall be kept in the vicinity of cylinders and conspicuously marked.
The alarm devices are in place and do not appear damaged.
Six monthly Inspection and Maintenance
CO2 lines to E/Room, Cargo holds/Paint Store (as applicable) shall be blown through with compressed air and recorded.
Annual Inspection and Maintenance
The boundaries of the protected space should be visually inspected to confirm that no modifications have been made to the enclosure that have created uncloseable openings that would render the system ineffective;
All storage containers should be visually inspected for any signs of damage, rust or loose mounting hardware. Cylinders that are leaking, corroded, dented or bulging should be hydrostatically retested or replaced;
System piping should be visually inspected to check for damage, loose supports and corrosion. Nozzles should be inspected to ensure they have not been obstructed by the storage of spare parts or a new installation of structure or machinery;
The manifold should be inspected to verify that all flexible discharge hoses and fittings are properly tightened; and all entrance doors to the protected space should close properly and should have warning signs, which indicate that the space is protected by a fixed carbon dioxide system and that personnel should evacuate immediately if the alarms | The manual release cabinet key shall be kept in the vicinity of cylinders and conspicuously marked.
Halon cylinder physical weighment or liquid level checks shall be carried out every two years (coinciding with safety equipment survey, if possible).

sound. All remote releasing controls should be checked for clear operating instructions and indication as to the space served.
Two-yearly Inspection and Maintenance
In addition to the above mentioned routine maintenance requirements, at least biennially (i.e. intervals of 2 years ± 3 months) in passenger ships or at each intermediate/periodical or renewal Safety Equipment (SEQ) survey in cargo ships, the following maintenance should be carried out
All high pressure cylinders and pilot cylinders should be weighed or have their contents verified by other reliable means to confirm that the available charge in each is above 90% of the nominal charge. Cylinders containing less than 90% of the nominal charge should be refilled. The liquid level of low pressure storage tanks should be checked to verify that the required amount of carbon dioxide to protect the largest hazard is available;
The discharge piping and nozzles should be tested to verify that they are not blocked. The test should be performed by isolating the discharge piping from the system and blowing dry air or nitrogen from test cylinders or suitable means through the piping.
Five-yearly Inspection and Maintenance
In addition to the above, at least biennially (intervals of 2 years ± 3 months) in passenger ships or at each renewal Safety Equipment (SEQ) survey in cargo ships, the following maintenance should be carried out by service technicians/specialists trained to standards accepted by the Administration:
Where possible, all activating heads should be removed from the cylinder valves and tested for correct functioning by applying full working pressure through the pilot lines. In cases where this is not possible, pilot lines should be disconnected from the cylinder- valves and blanked off or connected together and tested with full working pressure from the release station and checked for leakage. In both cases this should be carried out from one or more release stations when installed. If manual pull cables operate the remote release controls, they should be checked to verify the cables and corner pulleys are in good condition, move freely and, do not require excessive amount of travel to activate the system;
All cable components should be cleaned and adjusted as necessary, and the cable connectors should be properly tightened. If the remote release controls are operated by pneumatic pressure, the tubing should be checked for leakage, and the necessary charge of the remote releasing station pilot gas cylinders should be verified. All controls and warning devices should function normally, and the time delay if fitted, should prevent the discharge of gas for the required time period; and
After completion of the work, the system should be returned to service. All releasing controls should be verified in the proper position and connected to the correct control valves. All pressure switch interlocks should be reset and returned to service. All stop valves should be in the closed position.
Ten-yearly Inspection and Maintenance
High pressure cylinders should be subject to periodical tests at intervals not exceeding 10 years. At the 10-year inspection, at least 10% of the total number provided should be subjected to an internal inspection and hydrostatic test. If one or more cylinders fail, a total of 50% of the onboard cylinders should be tested. If further cylinders fail, all cylinders should be tested; | sound. All remote releasing controls should be checked for clear operating instructions and indication as to the space served.

All cable components should be cleaned and adjusted as necessary, and the cable connectors should be properly tightened. If the remote release controls are operated by pneumatic pressure, the tubing should be checked for leakage, and the necessary charge of the remote releasing station pilot gas cylinders should be verified. All controls and warning devices should function normally, and the time delay if fitted, should prevent the discharge of gas for the required time period; and
After completion of the work, the system should be returned to service. All releasing controls should be verified in the proper position and connected to the correct control valves. All pressure switch interlocks should be reset and returned to service. All stop valves should be in the closed position.
Ten-yearly Inspection and Maintenance
High pressure cylinders should be subject to periodical tests at intervals not exceeding 10 years. At the 10-year inspection, at least 10% of the total number provided should be subjected to an internal inspection and hydrostatic test. If one or more cylinders fail, a total of 50% of the onboard cylinders should be tested. If further cylinders fail, all cylinders should be tested;

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Hydrostatic testing for the fixed CO2 system shall be carried out at test facilities approved by the Chief Controller of Explosives in accordance with the Gas Cylinder Rules 2004, as amended, and as promulgated by the GOI. The test shall be witnessed and certificate endorsed by the ―Competent Person‖, if approved by the DGS and by a Surveyor of the Administration or recognized RO as the case may be, if the facility is not approved by the Directorate General of Shipping.
Test certificates, duly endorsed by the concerned surveyor must be provided and kept on board for inspections. Test date and pressure must be stamped on each bottle. This test shall not be carried out on board;
For subsequent 10-year services, alternation of the inspected cylinders must be carried out
i.e. different cylinders must be inspected from those done in the previous service, if 100% of them were not inspected during the previous in stance; and
Ships of 10 years or older coming into Indian flag will be required to carry this test at the next scheduled dry-docking.
All Flexible hoses should be replaced at the intervals recommended by the manufacturer and not exceeding every 10 years;
All discharge pipe lines shall be tested to a pressure of a maximum working pressure of the respective sections or as specified by the manufacturer, whichever is higher.

10.9.11.2 Water Mist Local Application System Maintenance Schedule (F.W. High pressure fixed fire fighting system fitted in E/R) where applicable

Weekly
Rotate the pump manually and ensure pump is free.
Press the ―Lamp test‖ to ensure bulbs are in working condition.

Monthly
Operate suction and delivery valve full shut to full open to ensure valves are not jammed.
Keep pump delivery valve shut. Operate manual call point & section valves for few seconds to ensure alarm present and pump starts. RESET from wheel house immediately. Alarm and pump stops. (Manual call point is in blue colour. Use the plastic small tool provided to activate the call point. There are six call points, test in a phased manner so that one cycle is completed in six month.)

Six Monthly
Blow through the system with compressed air to ensure nozzles are clear. (Open section valve manually, pump power off, delivery valve shut.)
Clean pump suction filter, if fitted.

10.9.11.3  External Water Spray System (Drench line) (where applicable)
System calculated by computer program. No manual adjustment to be made after installation. The nozzles are fitted with 1/2"npt and 2"bsp mail thread and various orifice openings. Each nozzle is individually calculated and marked for specific positions. Aft ship protected by one of high performance throw nozzle on each side. Emergency Fire Pump
The emergency fire pump is required to be available at any time or place for its ready use. The ship‘s crew is advised to ensure diligent use of checklist for the equipment. Emergency fire pumps shall be tried out regularly (weekly) so that the equipment is in full readiness at all times.
Annually – Test the emergency fire pump with isolation valves closed.
Manufacturer‘s manual shall be followed for routines time based maintenance of Emergency Fire Pump.

10.9.20   Inert Gas System for Methanol Tank
Being a very precise equipment much routine is not required. Filter element and activated carbon is required to replace as per running hrs. Maker manual can be consulted for the running hrs.
Following checks has to be done as per maker‘s manual:

Daily
Check drains trap operation.
Log process operating parameters
Dissemble and inspect drain traps

Monthly
Calibrate O2 analyser (Change fuel cell if necessary)

Quarterly
Inspect filter elements
Test alarm and shut down features
Verify setting and operation of pressure switch PS 25-1

Six Monthly
Replace F-11,F-12 and F-18 filter elements

Yearly
Inspect and clean instrumentation (pneumatic and electrical)
Test safety relief v/vs
Leak test pipe joints

4400 hrs./18 Monthly
Replace activated carbon in F-16

Fire Doors

Weekly
Verify all Fire Door control panel indicators (if provided) are functional by operating the lamp/indicator switch.

Quarterly
Test all Fire doors located in main vertical zone bulkheads for local operation.

Annual
Test all remotely controlled Fire doors for proper release.

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Weekly
Check that all valves have freedom of movement and are in correct position.
Check for freedom of movement of all monitors and secure them in ―parked‖ position.
Check level of foam liquid in main foam liquid sewerage tank.

Monthly
Check electric supply to foam liquid pump. Do not run pump dry.
Open sea water distribution valve and start sea water pump. Open monitor stop valve on furthest monitor and run for a few minutes ensuring that there is no trace of foam liquid in system and that monitor performance is satisfactory. Stop sea water pumps and return all valves to normal position.

Quarterly
Verify the proper quantity of foam concentrate is in the foam system storage tank.

Half Yearly
Refer to maker‘s operating instructions and produce foam from any one monitor only. Run system for approximately three minutes to ensure that satisfactory foam is produced and that system functions normally. Shut off system as per instructions.
Refer to maker‘s operating instructions – after use and comply – ensuring that all valves are returned to their normal positions.
Check level of foam liquid in main foam liquid storage tank and replenish as necessary.
Check foam liquid strainer and clean as necessary.

Yearly
Visually inspect all accessible components for proper condition;
Functionally test all fixed system audible alarms;
Flow test all water supply and foam pumps for proper pressure and capacity and confirm flow at the required pressure in each section (Ensure all piping is thoroughly flushed with fresh water after service.);
Test all system cross connections to other sources of water supply for proper operation;
Verify all pump relief valves, if provided, are properly set;
Examine all filters/strainers to verify they are free of debris and contamination;
Verify all control/section valves are in the correct position;
Blow dry compressed air or nitrogen through the discharge piping or otherwise confirm the pipe work and nozzles of high expansion foam systems are clear of any obstructions, debris and contamination. This may require the removal of nozzles, if applicable;
Samples of all foam concentrates carried on board are to be subjected to the periodical control tests as detailed below, and
Test all fuel shut-off controls connected to fire-protection systems for proper operation.

Five Yearly
Perform internal inspection of all control valves;
Flush all high expansion foam system piping with fresh water, drain and purge with air;
Check all nozzles to prove they are clear of debris; and | Weekly

Test all foam proportioners or other foam mixing devices to confirm that the mixing ratio tolerance is within +30 to -10% of the nominal mixing ratio defined by the system approval.
Portable Foam Applicator Monthly
Verify all portable foam applicators are in place, properly arranged, and are in proper condition.
Annual
Verify all portable foam applicators are set to the correct proportioning ratio for the foam concentrate supplied and the equipment is in proper order;
Verify all portable containers or portable tanks containing foam concentrate remain factory sealed, and the manufacturer's recommended service life interval has not been exceeded;
Portable containers or portable tanks containing foam concentrate, excluding protein based concentrates, less than 10 years old, that remain factory sealed can normally be accepted without the periodical foam control tests required in MSC.1/Circ.1312 being carried out,
Protein based foam concentrate portable containers and portable tanks should be thoroughly checked and, if more than five years old, the foam concentrate should be subjected to the periodical foam control tests required in MSC.1/Circ.1312, or renewed; and
The foam concentrates of any non-sealed portable containers and portable tanks, and portable containers and portable tanks where production data is not documented, should be subjected to the periodical foam control tests required in MSC.1/Circ.1312.
Testing of Foam Samples
Samples from all foam concentrates of carried onboard shall be subjected to the periodical control tests in accordance with MSC.1/Circ.1312, for low expansion foam, or MSC/Circ.670 for high expansion foam. Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Navigation Equipments
The Maker‘s manual and instructions book shall be referred in each specific case. Following basic guidelines for maintenance shall also be followed:

Standard Compass & Gyro Compass
Standard Compass
Gimbals shall be kept clean and greased for free movement. Liquid inside to be checked to remove any air bubbles. Standard compass shall be swung by the Master and a deviation curve made at least once in every twelve months.
The standard compass shall be adjusted by a qualified Compass Adjuster under the following circumstances
When inconsistency between two successive deviation curves observed.
After drydocking/structural alterations that could affect its permanent/induced magnetism.
Electrical/magnetic equipment close to the compass installed/removed.
Deviation curve and Compass adjustment certificate by the qualified Compass Adjuster shall be displayed in the wheelhouse.
Compass error book shall be maintained.

10.10.1.2  Gyro Compass
The headings of standard compass and gyro compass shall be compared every watch. The equipment shall be maintained/serviced as per manufacturer‘s instructions contained in the manual.

GPS/DGPS Navigator
Keep unit clean and dry.
Antenna to be kept clean.
The equipment shall be maintained/serviced as per manufacturer‘s instructions contained in the manual.

Echo Sounder
Ensure sufficient recording paper roll in the equipment and verify its feed is proper.
Check stylus for wear, replace when necessary.
Compare readings frequently with chart datum to ascertain reliability.
In dry-dock ensure transducer face is cleaned and not painted.
The equipment shall be maintained/serviced as per manufacturer‘s instructions contained in the manual.

10.10.4	Navtex Receiver
Check equipment has sufficient paper roll.
Conduct self test if provision exists.
Check antenna connection and keep antenna clean of dust, soot.
The equipment shall be maintained/serviced as per manufacturer‘s instructions contained in the manual. | Navigation Equipments

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.10.5	Radar
The equipment shall be maintained/serviced as per manufacturer‘s instructions contained in the manual. However, when using radar, the following shall be checked and logged:
the radar‘s overall performance
the identity of the fixed objects observed
gyro error and accuracy of the heading marker
the accuracy of variable range marker, bearing cursor and fixed range rings
on true motion check that the display is correctly stabilised
scanner mechanism shall be checked and oil replenished, if required.

10.10.6	Chronometer Daily
Check error by comparing with radio time signals or by GPS
Wind chronometers at fixed time (where applicable)

10.10.7	Aldis Lamp/Aldis Lamp Battery
Keep the battery charged, check voltage and operate lamp once a week.
Check electrolyte level and its specific gravity once a month. Add distilled water to restore the level. Never use Electrolyte for topping up.
Keep battery always clean. Apply petroleum jelly around the terminals to prevent corrosion, once in a month.
At least two spare bulbs shall be stored.

10.10.8   Automatic Identification System (AIS)
For operation of AIS, maker‘s manual shall be referred. AIS shall always be in operation when ships are underway or at anchor. However, AIS may be switched off in following situations:
when the Master believes that ship‘s information from AIS might compromise the safety or security of the ship.
during port stay if AIS shall be kept in low-power mode and/or switched off, as per the requirement of the port.

Whenever AIS is switched off while ship is underway/at anchor or in port, such action and the reason for doing so shall always be recorded in the ship‘s Deck Logbook. The Master shall restart the AIS on departure from the port and after restarting the AIS, data of own ship shall be verified with that of other vessels in the vicinity. Manufacturers‘ guidelines shall be followed for maintenance. AIS is a surveyable item during SRC survey.

10.10.9   Speed Log (where applicable)
A speed and distance measuring device, or other means, to indicate speed and distance over the ground in the forward and athwartship direction. Manufacturer‘s guidelines shall be referred for maintenance and periodic checks of the equipment.
When the vessel is in dry-dock, remove all the sea growths from the radiation surface of transducer without applying a strong shock to the radiation surface. | 10.10.5	Radar

Manufacturers‘ guidelines shall be followed for maintenance. AIS is a surveyable item during SRC survey.

10.10.9   Speed Log (where applicable)
A speed and distance measuring device, or other means, to indicate speed and distance over the ground in the forward and athwartship direction. Manufacturer‘s guidelines shall be referred for maintenance and periodic checks of the equipment.
When the vessel is in dry-dock, remove all the sea growths from the radiation surface of transducer without applying a strong shock to the radiation surface.

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.10.10	Fog Horn (Ship‘s Whistle)
Horn shall be tried out daily as per SMS Form: NAV003.
Quarterly insulation checks to be carried out.
Quarterly greasing of pulling wire to be done.

10.10.11	VDR/S-VDR
Vessels built after July 2002 are fitted with a VDR and existing vessels built prior thereto shall be fitted with a VDR (which may be an SVDR) by their next dry-docking after July 2006. Further, as per DGS requirement, VDR/SVDR shall have a float free capsule for easy recovery after an incident/accident. As the existing VDRs cannot be interfaced with a float free capsule, some vessels are fitted with a VDR as well as an SVDR with float free capsule to meet the requirements.
The purpose of a VDR is to maintain and store (in a secure and retrievable form) the information concerning the position, movement, physical status, command and control of a vessel over the period leading up to and following an incident, having an impact thereon. Information contained in a VDR/SVDR shall be made available to both the Administration and the Company. This information is for use during any subsequent investigation to identify the cause(s) of the incident. Since the equipment has facility to preserve a back up for 12 hours only, Master shall ensure that recorded data is stored safely and is available for analysis/reconstructing the scenario of sequences during the subsequent investigation, if any.

The VDR/SVDR has to undergo an annual performance verification test (APT) by an authorised service engineer during the annual safety equipment survey and the certificate needs to be preserved for one year.

VDR/SVDR shall have emergency source of electrical power. The unit should be entirely automatic in normal operation. Means should be provided whereby recorded data may be saved by an appropriate method following an incident, with minimal interruption to the recording process.

Back up Procedure
All radio officers/navigating officers, including the Master, shall familiarise themselves with the operation of VDR/SVDR, particularly how to take back up and retrieve the carry away memory module in case of an incident/accident. The information regarding procedure for back up and retrieval is provided in the instruction manual of the VDR/SVDR installed on board. The back up shall be taken and preserved (by transferring the data another computer memory) within 12 hours of the incident/accident. The back up is required by investigating authorities and/or P&I Clubs. Failure to provide this may go against the vessel even when not at fault. The back up information is recorded in a USB Memory Stick, special DVD ROM, PCIMA card or hard disk, depending on the type of VDR/SVDR. The latest VDR/SVDR is supplied with a password protected play back software CD. The CD with the password shall remain in custody of the Master‘s and shall be included in his Handing/Taking Over Report.
VDR/SVDR backup procedure to be displayed near equipment and on bridge. | 10.10.10	Fog Horn (Ship‘s Whistle)
Horn shall be tried out daily as per SMS Form: NAV003.
Quarterly insulation checks to be carried out.
Quarterly greasing of pulling wire to be done.

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.11    Communication Equipment & GMDSS Installation
Comply with maintenance requirements of GMDSS rules and regulations. The maintenance of GMDSS equipments shall be carried out as per Shore-Based Maintenance Contract (SBMC) approved by the Administration. Communication equipment shall also include walkie-talkies, two way VHF telephones. Maintenance schedule shall demonstrate weekly, monthly and routine inspection as suggested by the makers and found suitable and applicable to the vessel. Records of all such maintenance, inventory of spares shall be maintained.

Power Source (Ref. SOLAS Ch. IV)
Reserve source of power shall be independent of the ship‘s electrical system and this shall include supply of electric lighting to the installation.
Wherever a reserve source of energy consists of rechargeable accumulator batteries, a means of automatically charging such batteries shall be provided which shall be capable of recharging them to minimum capacity requirements within 10 hrs.

Maintenance of GMDSS Battery
On/Off load voltages checked daily and Entered in battery log.
Top up with distilled water, cleaning of all vents and terminals, applying petroleum jelly to terminals, putting the batteries on charge, monitoring and recording specific gravity after charge and making entry in the GMDSS battery log shall be done on monthly basis.
The capacity test of the batteries shall be done annually preferably when vessel moored safely along side.

Long Range Identification & Tracking (LRIT)
SOLAS Ch. V Reg. 19 requires every ship to automatically transmit the following long-range identification and tracking information:
The identity of the ship
The position of the ship (latitude and longitude)
The date and time of position provided
System and equipment used to meet the requirement of this regulation shall conform to the performance standards and functional requirement and be Type approved by the Administration.

The existing INMARSAT C equipment onboard used for GMDSS can be utilised for LRIT. To ensure that the ship borne equipment complies with the Regulations, the equipment shall be subjected to a Compliance Test. On successful testing, M/s. Tata Communication Ltd. are authorised to issue Conformance Test Reports on behalf of Administration. The certificate is in a format as prescribed by MSC Circ. 1307 and remains valid until the ship remains with the Flag.

In the event of an LRIT equipment is switched off for any reason such as dry-docking, lay up repairs or malfunction of the equipment, the ship shall inform LRIT National Data Centre (DG Shipping) – e-mail: lritndc@dgshipping.com, at the beginning as well as upon restoration of the system. | 10.11    Communication Equipment & GMDSS Installation

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Maintenance of Anchoring & Mooring Equipments
Mooring Winch/Windlass
The winches shall be lubricated at least once a month.
All pedestal bearings and other points covered under lubrication schedule shall be greased.
Lubricate the pin and threaded parts of the brake rod.
Lubricate the pinion and wheel gears with gear oil.
Check oil level in gear case as well as condition of gears.
Check foundation bolts, bearing holding down bolts, and studs connecting gypsy and gear wheel.
Check brake lining, renew if required.
Check brake band stoppers are in place and adjust the clearance.
Spare anchor crown pin, shackle shall be free and well greased.

Mooring Ropes
The Chief Officer and crew shall ensure that the ropes are cared for, utilised and maintained in line with industry best practices.

Mooring Rope Inspection
Mooring ropes shall be periodically inspected along their entire length at least once a month.
The wear along the rope shall be externally examined and areas of wear closely checked to assess the integrity of the ropes.
Eye splice integrity and eye wear shall be checked and the strands of the rope shall be opened up for checking internal wear.
Loose coils used on the bits shall be changed end for end once the working end becomes worn.
Major damage lengths should not be cropped out and replaced with short splice as this can reduce the strength of the rope.
If there is any doubt as to the strength and integrity of the rope, it should be replaced.
Ensure that test certificates and replacement dates are available on board.

Mooring Ropes Maintenance
Rope shall be properly stored away from wet deck, precipitation and direct sunlight; they should either be covered or stored below deck.
Mooring rollers, winch drum ends, bollards and panama leads shall be kept free for turning and should be free from damage/rust on the surface, which could cause rope wear.
Surging of rope on winch drum or slack away by rendering should be avoided.
Sharp angles in the lead of the rope shall be avoided between the fairleads and the mooring bollard on the wharf.

Mooring Fittings
Lubricate rotating parts such as roller or fair leads through grease nipple using grease gun every month.
Keep mooring rollers, bollards and warping drums/capstans free from corrosion to reduce damage to mooring lines. | Maintenance of Anchoring & Mooring Equipments

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.12.4	Hydraulic Plant for Deck Machinery

Weekly routine/prior use
The oil level in oil reservoir should be equivalent to 1/2 – 2/3 of net tank capacity, when the expansion tank is filled up with oil.
Check the oil level when the hydraulic pump is stopped after purging air from the branch and the main line.
Ensure that correct grade of oil is replenished.
Check and clean oil filters, and purge out air from system.

Monthly Routine
Check the oil level in oil tanks and ensure filters are clean.
Leakages in the hydraulic pump room, if any, shall be attended promptly.

10.12.5	Booby Hatch Cover
Lack of watertight integrity of hatch cover could endanger safety of the vessel.
Booby hatch cover shall be inspected every three months for water tightness, signs of corrosion, distortion or damages.
Hatch cover shall be hose tested after any repairs/at least once in three months.

10.12.6	Kamfork Winch (Shark Jaws) (where applicable)
Vessel shall carry out maintenance as per manufacturer instruction manuals. | 10.12.4	Hydraulic Plant for Deck Machinery

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
10.13	Pipelines and Valves
All pipelines shall be visually examined at least once in three months (particularly those vessels which are more than ten years old).
All pipelines shall be properly painted and shall be marked as follows:
Date and pressure test of bunker and fire pipelines shall be stencilled.
Pipeline intended for exhaust gas, Freon etc. shall be properly lagged.
Identification showing what fluid is flowing inside (Colour Code).
Direction of flow.
Any damage or mal-operation shall be noted for prompt rectification. If permanent repairs are not feasible immediately, cold repair shall be done till replacement is possible.
Ensure correct setting of valves and lines to avoid undue pressures.
Ensure that all clamps are properly fitted and not vibrating.
All valves shall have suitable identification.
All sea suction and overboard valves shall be tried out once a month for proper operation.
Maintenance Schedule Monthly
Visual inspection for signs of cracks, corrosion, damaged clamps or any other damage.
Check insulation, if provided and ensure the same is free of oil traces.
Check operation of valves and rectify leakages.
Visual inspection of gland studs of valves for corrosion, damage of threads etc. shall be carried out.
Check pressure gauges and thermometers etc. are in working order.
Lubricate all gearboxes for the valve operating mechanism especially in ballast and main sea water line valves, if provided.

2½ Yearly
Overhaul all critical valves including pressure relief valves.
Check and calibrate pressure gauges fitted on the lines.

During Dry-dock or Lay-up
Thorough overhaul, renewal as required, pressure testing of pipes and valves shall be undertaken. Painting of lines and valves shall be undertaken as required. All sea valves, sea suction and overboard valves shall also be overhauled and tested during dry-docking. Particular attention shall be paid to condition of overboard valves and stub pieces connecting the shell. | 10.13	Pipelines and Valves

Main Engine, Auxiliary Engine & (Bow/Stern/Azimuth) Thrusters
Main Engine & Auxiliary Engine Maintenance Plan
Planned maintenance schedule has been developed taking into consideration the manufacturer‘s maintenance instructions.
Maintenance routines (daily operation, every 500+ hours, 1000+ hours, 2000+ hours, 4000+ hours, 8000+ hours etc.) shall be carried out as per manufacturer‘s instructions following planned maintenance schedule. During maintenance/overhaul, inspection by Class surveyor shall be arranged for crediting CSM survey cycles, if falling due.
Duly filled in maintenance report shall be forwarded to the Operating Division every month.
Any alterations in the intervals of maintenance schedule shall be done with the concurrence of the Superintendent.
All safety precautions shall be observed while working with the machinery. Tally marks shall be noted while assembling the parts. All parts shall be tightened to the required level as prescribed by the makers — using specified lubricant on threads.

Bow Thruster Maintenance Plan
Bow thruster motor shall be checked in running condition for any abnormal sound when in use.
Oil tank level shall be checked every day.
Check the auxiliary and main servo pump units for proper function (pressures, abnormal sound, vibration etc.) monthly.
Check oil filter for clogging and condition of oil for any emulsification monthly.
Oil change shall be done in every dry-dock or earlier if emulsification/contamination noticed.

Stern Thruster Maintenance Plan (where applicable)
Stern thruster motor shall be checked in running condition for any abnormal sound when in use.
Oil tank level shall be checked every day.
Replace filter cartridge after first 100 hours of operation, after each oil renewal and further when indicated on the clogging indicator of the filter.
Check the auxiliary and main servo pump units for proper function (pressures, abnormal sound, vibration etc.) monthly.
Check oil filter for clogging and condition of oil for any emulsification monthly.
Oil change shall be done in every dry-dock or earlier if emulsification/contamination noticed.

10.15    Steering Gear
Chief Engineer Officer shall be responsible for maintaining the system in proper operational condition. Maintenance and overhauls shall be carried out as per Maker‘s instruction manuals.
Steering gear compartment shall be kept clean at all times. Ensure that no unwanted items are stored in the compartment.
Single, synchro and emergency mode (manual & auto mode) shall be tried out once a month.
Instructions regarding steering change over procedure to emergency mode to be prominently displayed in steering gear compartment and wheel house.

Every watch
Check Rudder Angle Indicator.

Daily at Sea
Check oil level in steering oil tank and the replenishing tank.
Check for leakages at hydraulic pumps, rams and at couplings of hydraulic lines.
Check for abnormal noise or vibration.
Check steering room ventilation system.
Check failure alarm.

Weekly
Check communication system between Engine Room/Bridge/Steering Compartment.
Lubricate telemotor linkages and other moving parts.
Check the hand-pump system for steering compartment bilges.
Check bilge high level alarm for proper functioning.

Monthly
Steering shall be tried out hard port to hard starboard with individual pumps as well as both pumps running.
Check emergency steering system.
Check steering header oil tank low level alarm.

Three Monthly
Check status of filters on hydraulic lines.
Check insulation of motors. Check contactor panel and carry out routine maintenance (i.e. clean contacts and check relays).
Ensure that all pressure gauges are operational. | 10.15    Steering Gear

10.16  Electrical Equipment and Instrumentation Maintenance (including testing and measuring equipment)
All electrical and electronic equipment on board shall be maintained by the Electrical Officer/Mechanist under the supervision of Chief Engineer Officer.
The navigation and radio equipment shall be maintained by Radio Officer. However, Electrical Officer/Mechanist shall ensure that correct and uninterrupted electrical supply is made available for the equipment.
Electrical Officer/Mechanist shall assist the Radio Officer/navigating officer for tracing and rectifying faults in electrical/electronic equipment on Bridge as and when required by the Master.

Electrical Equipment
All running electrical motors and starters, alternators, main switchboard and various distribution panels as well as the contactor panels shall be inspected every day.
Motor bearings shall be lubricated once in three months.
The fixed and moving contacts in contactor panels shall be inspected once in 3 months or if a fault develops earlier.
All cutouts, protective relays and preferential trips shall be checked for proper functioning once a year.
Main switchboard shall be cleaned during dry-dock and all connections shall be checked for tightness.
The conduit piping on deck shall be checked for any wastage/mechanical damage. The clamps securing conduit piping shall also be checked for proper fitment every three months.
All electrical fittings including light fittings on deck and in ER shall be properly secured. Missing/broken shades shall be replaced promptly. No loose or hanging wiring/electrical fitting shall be permitted.
Shore connection box and the circuit breaker shall be maintained in good order at all times, although the same is used only during dry dock.
Electrical hot plates and pantry boilers in galley shall be checked once a week for cleanliness and earth fault.
Crew engaged in galley shall be advised to avoid spillage of water and oil on these equipment. They shall also be conversant regarding switching off of the equipment.
Insulation of all electrical equipment, including spare motors on board, shall be checked and recorded once in three months.
Terminal boxes shall be made watertight. Cable entry/exit points shall be properly sealed.
The earth fault on main switchboard shall be checked every day.
Fuses of correct ratings shall be used.
All coupling guards and fan protective covers for the motors shall be fitted back after any maintenance work has been done. Any missing guards shall be restored.
Accuracy of all voltmeters, ammeters and frequency meters shall preferably be verified during scheduled dry dock/lay-up.
A list of equivalent/spare motors of each type shall be readily available so that in an emergency situation critical machinery can be maintained. | 10.16  Electrical Equipment and Instrumentation Maintenance (including testing and measuring equipment)

No maintenance or repair work shall be attempted unless the equipment has been effectively isolated and any stored energy is dissipated as in the case of condensers. Personnel safety shall be observed, such as display of warning notices, locking of circuit breakers, removal of fuses, use of insulated tools and use of safe testing instruments.
Insulation testing should only be carried out when no flammable gas mixture is present.
Safety Precautions while Servicing Electrical Equipment
In areas/compartments accommodating exposed live electrical wires/connections and switch boards following notice should be prominently displayed:





DANGER !!
HIGH VOLTAGE
In case of electrical accident, sound general emergency alarm.
While rescuing casualty as a result of electrocution, instructions contained in the ‗Ship Captain‘s Medical Guide‘ be implicitly followed.
Do not touch victim or live electrical source.
Disconnect power, if possible.
Use dry wood pole or rope to remove victim.
Resuscitate after rescue.
Testing & Measuring Equipment
All voltmeters, ammeters, frequency meters, AVO meters, Megger and such measuring instruments shall be function tested once a month.
Power supply shall be checked prior use.
Battery shall be replaced, if required (normal battery life is 2 - 2½ years).
Zero check. Meter must read Zero in non-measuring mode, with power on once in every three months.
Instrumentation
All meters/gauges, temperature gauges, sensors and pressure/temperature switches and alarm units on the following instrumentation panel shall be function tested once in three months for their proper functioning and operation. All indicator lamps on the panels shall also be checked daily and fused lamps replaced. All remote-reading gauges shall be tallied for proper reading in reference to the local meters once in six months and recorded.

Other Ancillary Equipment
Maintenance of ancillary equipment listed below shall be carried out in accordance with the instruction manual provided on board. However, basic guideline for some of the equipment is furnished below:

Bilge and Ballast System
Towards time-based routine maintenance, PMS shall be followed and reported.

Maintenance Programme for Oily Bilge Pump, Fire & G.S. Pump
Towards time-based routine maintenance, PMS shall be followed and reported every month to the operating division.

Maintenance Procedure for Pumps
Towards time-based routine maintenance of various salt water and fresh water centrifugal pumps, PMS shall be followed and reported.

Maintenance of Ship & Its Equipments | 
Air Compressors & Air Pressure Vessels
Towards time-based routine maintenance of air compressors and air pressure vessels, PMS shall be followed and reported.

Air Compressor Type HL2/105 – Emergency Compressor (where applicable)
The following guidelines shall be followed by the vessel for a normal routine maintenance.

After the first 200 hours operations
Change lubrication oil. Drain the sump while the oil is warm, clean the sump thoroughly before filling with fresh oil.

Daily inspection
Make a quick general inspection of the whole compressor (in normal operation) and specially check the following:
Lubricating oil level
Compressed air temperature and pressure
Automatic equipment

Overhaul Routine A (1.000 running hours or every 2 years)
Make sure that overhaul kit no.3036MK2 are in stock before starting overhaul of compressor according to routine A – 1.000 hours service. Please follow installation instructions included in the kit.
Replace lubricating oil.
Remove the valves from both cylinders. Check for carbon deposits. Dismantle the valve for cleaning and repair if necessary. Use spare part kit no.3036MK2 and 3037MK2 to overhaul valves. All valve gaskets should be replaced with new parts at assembly.
Inspect the flexible coupling between compressor and motor.
Check all bolts and nuts for proper tightness. Also check vibration dampers and hose connections if the unit is flexible mounted. Check that no oil has come in contact with rubber elements in the vibration dampers.
Function – test the safety valve. start the compressor, and slowly close the stop valve on the compressed air line. The air pressure should not exceed max. Working pressure + 10%. The safety valves are sealed and the setting should not be adjusted. If the valves are malfunctioning or open at wrong pressure, the safety valves should be replaced.
Check all the pipe connections. (compressor running)
Check that all automatic equipment is functioning correctly.
Change suction air filter (Part no.8451)
The vessel shall follow overhaul routine 5000+ running hours & 10000+ running hours as per instruction manual for above compressor.

10.17.5	Domestic Fridge & Air Conditioning Plants
Routine maintenance shall be carried out as per maker‘s instruction manual. Due care shall be taken to prevent accidental release of refrigerant gases (refer section 7.2.3.10) | Air Compressors & Air Pressure Vessels

10.17.8   Provision Handling Crane/Lifting Equipment
Detailed instructions for maintenance of crane(s) furnished in maker‘s instruction manual shall be followed.
Provision crane and chain blocks shall be lubricated prior use. Safe working loads shall be clearly marked and not exceeded while in use.
Testing shall include, but not limited to, checking of limit switches, cable insulation, magnetic brake operation and trial of all crane movements. Records of such tests shall be maintained in Maintenance Register.
Crane shall be examined/tested annually/5-yearly, in compliance with Dock Safety Regulations.

10.17.9   EVAC System (where applicable)
The EVAC Online Vac shall be serviced at regular intervals according to operating and maintenance instructions to guarantee reliably function over a long period of time. Therefore, these maintenance instructions must be available and followed by operators and maintenance staff at all times.
Ensure that there is a free circulation of the cooling air. Do not cover the EVAC Online VAC unit or pumps. | 10.17.7	Shaft Generator Every Month

10.17.12	Ship‘s Crane (where applicable as in PSV)
All precaution as per maker‘s manual recommendation is to be followed.
Maintenance log to be maintained, all maintenance, abnormal observation, repair should be logged.
Filter element has to be removed as indicator revealed bad condition, at least once in a year.
Procedure for renewal of hydraulic oil to be followed.
Grease all the suggest in TTS manual, follow lubrication chart and lubrication schedule in this regard.
Slew and winch gear oil to be charge at every 1000 hrs of crane running.
Slew ring wear has to be done annually and should be logged down in the crane log. Please follow maker‘s recommendation in this regard.
Maintenance log is to be maintained and include the log in monthly return. | Sewage Treatment Plant (where applicable)

Yearly
Check the alignment of the coupling halves. Preferably immediately after ending operation, while the temperature is still at operating level.
Check capacity and absorbed horse power. Capacity and power loss will indicate wear.
Screw shafts and cylinder must be checked for damage.
Check the screw flank clearance as well as clearance between the timing gears.
Every 4000 hrs and 5000 hrs.
The axial clearance of he bearing is to be checked.
If the clearance between the timing gears is more than 0.5 mm/.0020‖ timing gear should be replaced.

10.18.14	Hot Water Boiler (where applicable) Weekly
Water level should be checked and refill water if necessary.
Check the flame through inspection glass when burner is running and make adjustment if necessary.

Monthly
Fuel oil filter on the line and filter in oil p/p shall be cleaned.
Check through the inspection glass when the burner is running, if it is coke residue in combustion chamber, the boiler shall be cleaned.

Yearly
Dismount the burner and the burner plate/cleaning doors.
Remove the burner/burner plate and the cleaning doors and clean the boiler with a brush or cleaning liquid.
Check ceramic plates on the burner plate, if the plates are worn they have to be changed. check gasket for the cleaning doors, change gasket if necessary.
Check the burner tube. Clean the tube if necessary.
Dismount the burner insert, clean parts and change nozzles.
Check air inlet and blower wheel, clean if necessary.
Check the set point for the thermostate and pressure switch.
Check that the safety v/vs are not leaking.

10.19    Maintenance of Testing and Measuring Equipment
All testing and measuring equipment used on board shall be verified for accuracy and proper functioning.
Measuring instruments or gauges and thermometers of essential machineries and equipments (e.g. pressure vessels/lines, electrical power plant, firing and combustion installations) to be calibrated during the planned lay-up of the vessel or prior to survey as per the requirements of applicable rules and regulations.
Proper record of calibration shall be maintained by Chief Engineer Officer/Chief Officer.

Pneumatic Tank Gauging System
Turn by hand and check the 4-way change over cock at the time of operation.
Check the closing of the orifice for the air unit, and depress the button for cleaning of orifice at the time of operation.
Take the air filter element for air supply unit and wash it by solvent like trichloroethyl.
Check for any leakage at the time of operation.
Check, by pressure gauge at second side for decompressor valve. The set pressure should be maintained. Check and replace the interior diaphragm spring if necessary.

Catalytic Filament Combustible Gas Detector
Before Use		Check sampling hose condition, all connecting points, sealing of unit
Carry out function test.
Calibrate for zero and span.
Check power source, recharge batteries, if required.
Purge the unit thoroughly and clean filters.
After Use		Purge, clean and store.

Portable Oxygen Analyser
Before Use		Carry out function test
Check power source, recharge batteries, if required
Calibrate for zero and span*
Purge the unit thoroughly and clean filters. After Use		Remove batteries, if not in use
Every 3 Years		Check sampling hose condition, all connecting points and sealing of unit
Replace sensor, heater element, fuse as per maker‘s instructions

*	O2 Analyser accuracy to be checked before use by purging with atmospheric air and ensuring reading is 21% by volume.

Maintenance, Calibration & Test Procedures
All portable gas measurement instruments should have a valid calibration certificate and should be tested strictly in accordance with the manufacturer‘s instructions before use.
Calibration to be carried out annually by shore-based agency. | 10.19    Maintenance of Testing and Measuring Equipment

Oily Water Separator (OWS)
The oily water separator pumping and disposal system shall have arrangement to lock the overboard discharge valve.
Ship‘s personnel, who performed the task shall make entries in the Tank Sounding Log, Oil Record Book. Oil Record Book shall be examined and signed by Chief Engineer Officer and/or the Master. The instructions on the cover page of the Oil Record Book shall be followed.

External inspection and general check
Pipeline leakage

To check function of oil water interface detector.

The oily water separator pumping and disposal system shall have arrangement to lock the overboard discharge valve.
Ship‘s personnel, who performed the task shall make entries in the Tank Sounding Log, Oil Record Book. Oil Record Book shall be examined and signed by Chief Engineer Officer and/or the Master. The instructions on the cover page of the Oil Record Book shall be followed.

Daily		Check parameters while running
External inspection and general check
Pipeline leakage
To flush with sea water after use Weekly		To clean suction strainer (line filter)
Lubricate all moving parts
Check mechanical freeness of pump
Monthly		To clean sensor and check 15 ppm alarm and zero setting (if fitted)
Check Electrical systems and test all alarms 3 Monthly		To check solenoid valves for all stages
6 Monthly		To remove and clean oil water interface detector.
To check function of oil water interface detector.
Clean coalescent filter/baffle plate, if required.
Yearly		To comply with the requirement of Annual/Intermediate survey.

Development of Safety Management System (SMS) Manuals
The Company has structured and documented Safety Management System manuals enabling the Company personnel to effectively implement the Company‘s safety, occupational health and environmental protection policy. The structure of the manuals has been mentioned in the matrix — Section 11.2.2.
For the purpose of effective ISM implementation, relevant extracts of the Company SMS Manual have been incorporated in the shipboard manual. Hence, only shipboard manuals shall be maintained on vessels for ISM compliance.
The Company SMS Manual and all Shipboard SMS Manuals (ship type wise) document procedures for all elements of the ISM Code, as detailed in Section 11.2.2, except the following:
ISM Code Ref. 13 – Certification & Periodical Verification — relates to the functions under the control of the Administration.
ISM Code Ref. 14 – Interim Certification — relates to the functions under the control of the Administration.
ISM Code Ref. 15 – Verification — relates to the functions under the control of the Administration.
ISM Code Ref. 16 – Forms of Certificates — relates to the functions under the control of the Administration.

11.1.2   Online Availability of Safety Management System (SMS) Manuals
Under SET-IT project, the process of uploading the SMS manuals for online use by the ships and the shore personnel is under progress. Subsequent to completion and satisfactory trial of the online system, the SMS manuals will be available online only, as a result whereof all hard copies of manuals will be withdrawn. Amendments to the manuals, as well as. SMS returns will thereafter be carried out online. | Documentation

11.1.3   Custodian of SMS Manuals
The DPA is the custodian of all the SMS Manuals along with all the certificates and testimonials associated thereto. The DPA is the authority who controls corrections/ amendments to the SMS Manuals arising out of considerations to changes in fleet, trade, new regulations and environmental requirements, reviews, internal and external audits onboard vessels and in the shore offices, changes required in SMS as a result of incidents and accidents in fleet and in industry in general. The original of respective SMS Manuals is retained in his custody whereas the copies get circulated to responsible officers onboard vessels and ashore, as per the distribution list. | 11.1.3   Custodian of SMS Manuals

Preparation and amendments of SMS Manuals shall be carried out in the manner as shown in the flow chart above.
A standard Company‘s formatted page shall be used for preparing the SMS Manual. The formatted page of the SMS manual shall be identified as controlled document and shall contain the following details:
Index	–	Indicating the section of the SMS Manual
Page	–	Page number of the total number of pages under that sub- section
Prep.	–	Initials of the person(s) who has/have prepared the section
Appr.	–	Initials of the person approving the section
Date	–	Indicating the date of the latest revision
Rev.	–	Indicating status of current revision number in force
The issue date will be as per the date indicated in the transmittal note. The effective date of the concerned SMS procedures shall be the date within fifteen days after receipt of such documents. In an existing SMS the enforcement date will be only for the revised procedures. Should any SMS procedures require to be enforced with immediate effect, the Company shall communicate to all concerned by separate notice or instructions by quickest means, and also indicate the date of enactment and validity for such instructions.
Preparation/Amendment and Despatch of SMS Documents
SMS Manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS Manuals concerning respective department and area of operation shall be prepared in the respective department by the responsible employee, under the supervision of the Departmental Head. The final draft of the SMS manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS manuals shall be submitted to the DO/DPA as applicable. If necessitated, concerned DO may also initiate proposal of amendments to SMS manuals. | SMS Document Control

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Documentation | 
The DO shall review the final draft of the SMS Manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS Manuals. If, during the process of this review, the DO finds that corrections/amendments are required, the draft shall be returned to the Departmental Head for effecting the same. On satisfactory completion of review, the DO shall submit the final draft of the SMS Manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS Manuals to the DPA.
The DPA shall assess the final draft of the SMS Manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS Manuals to ensure its suitability with the requirements of the SMS as a whole. While assessing, DPA convenes meetings of a group or discusses in the subsequent CSMC or SRC meetings, comprising of departmental heads/group in-charge, DOs and concerned responsible technical personnel. On satisfactory completion of the assessment, the DPA shall approve and arrange to issue the SMS Manuals or proposed amendments for distribution. Issuance of SMS manuals/documents, amendments will be done under a Transmittal Note (Form: DOC001) from the DPA‘s office. Despatch of SMS documents for C&MD‘s office, Directors, Regional Offices and new building vessels, is undertaken by DPA‘s office. Documents related to the Company‘s SMS to all other concerned, as per controlled circulation list is despatched through the DOs of respective Divisions. Shipboard related SMS documents shall be despatched to concerned Group I/C for onward distribution. The Transmittal Note shall be acknowledged by the recipient of the SMS manuals/documents, amendments and sent back to the ISM Cell. DO of each division shall liaise with the concerned Group I/C and monitor timely despatch to each ship of the division.
On receipt of such documents on board, the Master shall carry out necessary changes/ replacements as per the Transmittal Note, sign the acknowledgement and send it back to the respective DOs. DOs shall forward the same to the DPA‘s office for records.
SMS documents shall be annually reviewed and corrections incorporated, if considered necessary. Minor changes, such as telephone numbers, addresses, names, functional titles or issues affecting any procedures documented in the SMS shall be communicated through temporary instructions by the DPA and later included in the corrections/amendments of SMS documents, if found necessary during the annual review.
Corrections and amendments shall be based on:
Review results (Refer Verification and Review Section of the SMS Manual).
Feed back reports from ships/departments, accident investigation and operational experience.
Fleet/personnel/external changes.
DPA‘s temporary instructions required to be made permanent.
Circulars required to form part of the system.
Various ship inspection and audit reports.
Industry guidelines, relevant international and national rules and regulations
After the corrections/amendments are made, that part of the document shall be given a new revision number and effective date. The record of revision status will be maintained on the revision sheet included under section 11.1 of the Shipboard SMS Manual. The revised pages along with the revision sheet will be sent to the holder of the manual.
The recipient shall remove and destroy the old pages from the document and insert the new ones. Acknowledgement of such action shall be made, by forwarding the acknowledgement part of Transmittal Note (Form: DOC001) to the DO of the division, who shall send it to ISM Cell for records.
Whenever major revisions are carried out, ISM Cell may send entire revised manual under a Transmittal Note, instead of sending too many loose revised sheets. Recipient of the manual shall insert Revision Sheets (B) from old manual into the new revised manual for continuity and record and destroy the old manual making official log entry or send the same back to ISM Cell, as per instructions in the Transmittal Note. | The DO shall review the final draft of the SMS Manuals or proposed amendments to the SMS Manuals.  | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Documentation | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Documentation |  |  | 
In case of any change or inclusion of ship specific procedures required to be enforced with immediate effect in order to have an effective functioning of the SMS, such procedures may be promulgated under DPA‘s temporary instructions, as described under section 7 — Shipboard Operations of SMS Manual. These temporary instructions will be valid till the time the same are reviewed and included in the SMS during the revision of the Shipboard SMS manuals.
In case correction/amendment of the Shipboard SMS Manuals is deemed necessary by the Master, which need not be effected immediately and sent as a feed back for the improvement of the system, he shall forward his recommendations to the DO of the Division. The DO shall review the Master‘s recommendations, along with the concerned Departmental Head and if deemed necessary, initiate the procedure of preparation and incorporation of such amendments, as described within this section.
Unauthorized correction/amendments or marking of the SMS manuals shall not be made by any user of the manual. All correction/amendments shall comply with the procedure described.
Two complete sets (hard copies) of Shipboard Safety Management System (SMS) Manual shall be available onboard, one set with the Master and the other set with the Chief Engineer Officer. The hard copies of the manual shall be duly stamped with the rank of the holder, as means of identification.
In addition, four nos. Compact Discs (CDs), each containing the entire manual shall be available on board the vessel with Master, Chief Engineer Officer, Chief Officer and Second Engineer Officer. The CDs shall be signed by the DPA as a confirmation of controlled document. These CDs shall be duly stamped with the rank of the holder, as means of identification.
These manuals and CDs shall be available on board throughout the period that the vessel is in service as part of the Company fleet and shall be included in the Handing/Taking Over Reports of respective officers.

The procedure for preparation, correction/amendment, review, approval and distribution of standard forms and checklists used in the SMS shall also be controlled as detailed above.

The CDs shall be signed by the DPA as a confirmation of controlled document. These CDs shall be duly stamped with the rank of the holder, as means of identification.
These manuals and CDs shall be available on board throughout the period that the vessel is in service as part of the Company fleet and shall be included in the Handing/Taking Over Reports of respective officers.
Control of Standard Formats
The procedure for preparation, correction/amendment, review, approval and distribution of standard forms and checklists used in the SMS shall also be controlled as detailed above.
Controlled Circulation List
SMS Manuals shall be distributed as per the following manner: | In case of any change or inclusion of ship specific procedures required to be enforced with immediate effect in order to have an effective functioning of the SMS, such procedures may be promulgated under DPA‘s temporary instructions, as described under section 7 — Shipboard Operations of SMS Manual. These temporary instructions will be valid till the time the same are reviewed and included in the SMS during the revision of the Shipboard SMS manuals.
In case correction/amendment of the Shipboard SMS Manuals is deemed necessary by the Master, which need not be effected immediately and sent as a feed back for the improvement of the system, he shall forward his recommendations to the DO of the Division. The DO shall review the Master‘s recommendations, along with the concerned Departmental Head and if deemed necessary, initiate the procedure of preparation and incorporation of such amendments, as described within this section.
Unauthorized correction/amendments or marking of the SMS manuals shall not be made by any user of the manual. All correction/amendments shall comply with the procedure described.

11.3	Publications
The vessel shall carry adequate and up-to-date charts, sailing directions, list of lights, and Admiralty list of radio signals, nautical almanac, tide tables, notices to mariners and all other nautical publications necessary for the intended voyage; in compliance with SOLAS Chapter V.
In addition, the Company has established a list of standard publications that shall be carried on board by all vessels of the fleet. These publications are for reference by personnel on board. These publications are essential reference publications, regulations, rules, codes and standards. These publications shall be indexed with the ‗Code‘ provided against each title, hereunder.

The Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these publications. Publications‘ designated location in the wheelhouse shall be under the direct charge of the Chief Officer. Publications‘ designated location in the Radio Room shall be under the direct charge of the Radio Officer. Publications‘ designated location by rank of the ship‘s officer shall be under the direct charge of the respective officer. These shall be maintained under handing/taking over records of concerned officers.

Master shall consult the concerned Superintendent and Group in-Charge to endeavour that the up-to-date editions of these publications are available on board.

The Company identifies the need of carrying up-to-date books and publications on board for the intended voyage as per recommended list of publications included herewith.

The Master shall obtain information regarding new or revised publications from the DO. The Master shall place an emergency indent for the required publications, to the vessel‘s attending superintendent.

The Company may provide vessel with other publications not included under SMS. These shall be maintained under handing/taking over records of the concerned officer.

A list showing the record and distribution of all publications prescribed under Safety Management System and including additional publications related to ship‘s operation must be kept updated and readily available with Master.

11.4	Drawings
In addition to various other drawings required by the vessel's Deck, Engine, Radio departments, the vessel shall maintain the following or similar drawings to fulfil the requirements of the Shipboard SMS.
These drawings shall be indexed with the ‗Code‘ provided against each title, as shown hereunder. The Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these drawings. Drawings‘ designated location by rank of the ship‘s officer shall be under the direct charge of the respective officer and be maintained under their handing/taking over records.

The vessel may be in possession of, or Company may provide vessel with, additional drawings not included under SMS. These shall be maintained under the handing/taking over records of the officers in possession of respective drawings.

Vessels built prior to the implementation of Safety Management System may not have been supplied by the building yard with drawings having specific names as noted in the list, equivalent drawing(s) from the building yard shall be acceptable for the purpose. In some offshore vessels where the drawings specified under SMS are not available due to reasons mentioned above ship specific list of drawings shall be made, kept on board and maintained. The vessel specific revised drawing list shall be forwarded to the Operating Division.

A list showing the record and distribution of all drawings prescribed under Safety Management System and including additional drawings related to ship‘s operation must be kept updated and readily available with the Master and Chief Engineer Officer.

11.5	Manuals
The vessel shall maintain the following manuals to fulfill the requirements of the Shipboard SMS. In addition Company/manufacturers may provide various other manuals for the equipment in vessel's deck, engine, and radio departments. Manuals must be maintained under handing/taking over records of respective officers.
Manuals referred to in SMS shall be indexed with the ‗Code‘ provided against each title, as shown hereunder. The Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these manuals. Manuals‘ designated location in the wheelhouse shall be under the direct charge of the Chief Officer. Manuals‘ designated location in the radio room shall be under the direct charge of the Radio Officer.

Manuals located in the off/crew recreation rooms shall be under the direct charge of the Chief Officer.

Manuals have been assigned codes for standardisation across the operating division. Applicability on individual ship is subject to equipment being supplied/fitted on board.

A list showing the record and distribution of all manuals prescribed under Safety Management System and other manuals related to ship‘s operation/machinery must be kept updated and readily available with Master and Chief Engineer Officer.

11.6	Charts and Nautical Publications
The Chief Officer shall be responsible to the Master for ensuring that all charts and nautical publications are maintained in good order and, where relevant, corrected up-to-date. Chart Correction Log and Folio Index – BA shall be used to record the corrections made.
Corrections applicable to charts and nautical publications shall be obtained from Notices to Mariners. The Company has arrangements with their approved chart vendors to provide weekly (BA Charts) and fortnightly (Indian Charts) Notices to Mariners to Company‘s vessels.

The Master shall inform concerned superintendent, in the event of not receiving the Notices to Mariners, for taking necessary action. | 11.6	Charts and Nautical Publications

11.7	Certificates
The vessel shall maintain the following certificates (as applicable) to fulfil the requirements of the Shipboard SMS.
These certificates shall be indexed with the ‗Code‘ provided against each title, as shown hereunder. Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these certificates. Master shall verify and ensure that all certificates issued are duly signed and stamped. Certificates shall be duly endorsed after any periodical or annual surveys are carried out.
Certificates‘ designated location in the wheelhouse shall be under the direct charge of the Chief Officer.
Certificates‘ designated location in the radio room shall be under the direct charge of the Radio Officer/Officer assigned responsibilities by the Master.
Certificates‘ designated location by rank of the ship‘s officer shall be under the direct charge of the respective officer and be maintained under their handing/taking over records.
In addition, any other certificates, including builder‘s certificates for important machineries and equipments held on board, shall be maintained under handing/taking over of records of officer in-charge of the relevant equipment.

A list showing the record and distribution of all certificates, prescribed under Safety Management System, and other certificates related to ship‘s operation/machinery held on board, must be kept updated and readily available with Master and Chief Engineer Officer. This updated list of certificates shall be sent to the superintendent every month.

11.8	Circulars
From time to time the SIRIUS provides operational feedback to the fleet in the form of circulars. The circulars are issued in two volumes:
Fleet Circulars (Guidelines)
Fleet Circulars (Case-Studies)
These circulars contain operational feedback regarding marine operations, navigation, machinery operations, safety and general subjects. These circulars are prepared by T&OS Division. Whenever any circular contains instructions concerning Safety, Occupational Health & Environmental Protection and subjects covered by the Company‘s SMS, draft of such circular shall be sent to the DPA for review and assessment before final issue to the fleet.
Circulars shall be maintained in circular files listed in Section 11.9. Circulars are identified by the following:
Description
Index	–	Indicating the section of the Fleet Circular
Page	–	Page number of the total number of pages under that circular
Prep.	–	Initials of the person(s) preparing the circular
Appr.	–	Initials of the person approving the Circular
Date	–	Indicating the date of the latest revision
Rev.	–	Indicating status of current revision number in force
Circulars issued during the preceding year are reviewed by ISM Cell and instructions regarding these Circulars are issued by the DPA, along with fresh Table of Contents (if necessary), encompassing the revision in the Circulars. Table of Contents indicates the Circular retained after the review by ISM Cell.

Instructions regarding earlier Circulars
Circulars, where no revision number is indicated, the revision status to be read as 00.
Sr. No. and Con. No. indicated in circulars to be disregarded. | 11.8	Circulars

11.9	Files
In addition to files required for vessel‘s wage accounting, deck, engine, radio, purser, saloon departmental filing system, the vessel shall maintain following files to fulfil the requirements of the Shipboard SMS. These files shall be indexed with the ‗File No.‘ provided against each file, as shown in the list given hereunder. The Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these files. Maintenance of the respective files is the responsibility of the officer indicated in the list. These files shall form part of Handing/Taking over records of respective officers. Besides files listed below, any other ship-specific files if required to be maintained by an individual officer, this should be done in consultation with the Departmental Head. The Departmental Head shall maintain a master list of the files maintained by individual officer and such master list shall also be included by the respective officers in their handing/taking over reports.
Whenever a particular file is required to be divided in different parts because of its voluminous contents, it will be divided under the same file number by giving part number with stroke (/) after the file number e.g. 101/1, 101/02 where 1, 2 indicate the part number of the same file.

Retention Period
Files must be retained for the duration of period indicated under the column ‗Retention Period‘ against respective files. On completion of retention period, whenever a file is closed, the new file should contain records of preceding year for reference and continuity. All closed files are to be stored separately or dealt with as per instructions of the shore office. | 11.9	Files

11.10    Registers and Logs
In addition to various other registers/logs required for the vessel's wage accounting, deck, engine, radio, purser, saloon departments, the vessel shall maintain the following registers/ logs (subject to equipment being fitted) to fulfil the requirements of the Shipboard SMS.
Registers and logs shall be retained for the current year and three previous years.

The registers/logs, whose names are appended with a # sign, shall be retained during the period that the vessel is in service, as a part of the Company fleet.

The Master has the overall responsibility of the upkeep of these registers/logs. Registers/logs designated location in the wheelhouse shall be under the direct charge of the Chief Officer. Registers/logs designated location in the radio room shall be under the direct charge of the Radio Officer/Officer assigned responsibilities by the Master. Registers/logs designated location by rank of the ship‘s officer shall be under the direct charge of the respective officer.

Registers/logs shall form part of handing/taking over records of respective officers.

Verification, Review & Evaluation | 
Verification, Review & Evaluation

Safety Management System Internal Audit Procedure
Safety Management System Internal Audits of the Company, Division(s) and ships shall be carried out to verify whether safety, occupational health and pollution prevention activities comply with the SMS.
Company shall ensure the effective implementation of safety management system on board in its newly acquired vessels owned or technically managed vessels. In doing so company shall ensure the following tests and checks are carried out and recorded as applicable which includes but not limited to the following.
Assign superintendent and DO for the type of vessel.
Superintendent and DO are properly briefed when the vessel is inducted in company‘s fleet at the building yard.
Officers are posted in accordance with SMD after briefing at respective operational division and ISM/ISPS Cell.
Shipboard SMS manual and SSP (draft copy) are available on board. CSR and SSP are submitted to DGS for approval and proof of submission is available on board.
Approved booklets & manuals, plans & drawings, certificates (statutory and regulatory) are on board and kept in respective files and folders.
Policy and safety posters, instructions, safety signs & symbols, muster cards are displayed in respective locations.
Copies of latest charts and publications, notices to mariners are available.
All registers opened including safety register, LSA/FFA, ISPS etc. as per the list under section 11.10.
All LSA/FFA equipments are in working order. Abandon ship drill is carried out and record is available.
ISPS equipments are installed/placed on board as per requirements and test record is available.
Pollution prevention equipments i.e. IOPP and ISPP etc. are in working order complying with MARPOL ANNEXES.
Oil Record Book, Garbage Record Book and Garbage Management Plan are available onboard.
Safe Working Practices and Drug & Alcohol Policy are implemented and records available.
Medical accessories and medicines as per requirements are available and kept in respective places.
Effective housekeeping and hygiene maintenance of the vessel.
ISM/ISPS external and internal audit plans are made and appropriate application is submitted to the concern authorities.

The Safety Management System Internal Audits of the Company, Division and ships shall be carried out at least once a year and same shall be carried out within the window period of three months before previous audit date i.e. interval between two successive internal audits, ashore and on board, shall not exceed twelve months. Safety Management System Internal Audit Procedure
Safety Management System Internal Audits of the Company, Division(s) and ships shall be carried out to verify whether safety, occupational health and pollution prevention activities comply with the SMS.
Company shall ensure the effective implementation of safety management system on board in its newly acquired vessels owned or technically managed vessels.
