The Safety Management System Internal Audits of the Company, Division and ships shall be carried out at least once a year and same shall be carried out within the window period of three months before previous audit date i.e. interval between two successive internal audits, ashore and on board, shall not exceed twelve months. Only in exceptional circumstances,

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Verification, Review & Evaluation | 
with DPA‘s concurrence, this interval of twelve months may be exceeded, but not more than three months.
If necessary, DPA may arrange additional Internal Audit for evaluation of the effectiveness of the Safety Management System.
The ―Company Internal Audit‖ shall cover the Fleet Personnel Department, Purchase & Services Department, Chennai Regional Office, Kolkata Regional Office, Port Blair Branch Office and Haldia Branch Office and the Chairman & Managing Director of the Company.

The ―Divisional Internal Audit‖ shall cover L&PS Division, B&T Division and Offshore Department of T&OS Division.

The Safety Management System Auditor shall be independent of areas being audited and shall, as far as practicable, have undergone a recognised internal auditor‘s course, sufficiently experienced with the Company‘s technical operations of vessels and well conversant with the Safety Management System.

Corrective action for non-conformities arising out of internal audits shall be completed within a time period agreed to between the Auditor and the Auditee. Non-conformity Report, duly signed by the auditee, will constitute acceptance of non-conformity by the auditee. Normally, the time period agreed for completion of corrective action shall not exceed three months from the date of issuance of non-conformity. Only in exceptional cases, Auditor may put up departmental request for extension of agreed time period to the DPA for his consideration.

First Internal SMS Audit of newly inducted vessel
Whenever new ship types are to be added to an existing Document of Compliance and when a Company takes on responsibility for the operation of a ship which is new to the Company or when a ship changes the Flag, the First Internal Audit (SMS) to be carried out within three months of Interim Safety Management Certificate's issuance date.

Annual Audit Planning
DPA shall prepare the annual audit plan (Ref. Form: AUD001), which shall be provided to all DOs for necessary information and implementation. DPA shall identify the Internal Safety Management Auditor(s) for conducting audits as per plan. The Internal Safety Management System Auditor shall be independent of areas being audited and shall, as far as practicable, have done a recognised internal auditor‘s course, sufficiently experienced with the Company‘s technical operations of vessels and well conversant with the Safety Management System.

Preparation of Audit Schedule
The Internal Safety Management Auditor shall prepare the audit schedule in order to plan the execution of the audit (Ref. Form: AUD002).

Audit Execution
The Internal Safety Management Auditor shall collect objective evidence in a planned and systematic way. | with DPA‘s concurrence, this interval of twelve months may be exceeded, but not more than three months.
If necessary, DPA may arrange additional Internal Audit for evaluation of the effectiveness of the Safety Management System.

 | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Verification, Review & Evaluation | 

Interview of personnel shall be for the purpose of collecting and noting information. By receiving information from different sources, the auditor shall collate evidence in a precise manner in order to determine conformance to the SMS and possible improvements.
The Internal Safety Management Auditor shall:
Have a meeting with the audit team members, if any, to plan the audit
Have an opening meeting with the Auditee(s), discuss and agree the details of the audit schedule and availability of persons to be interviewed.
Prepare the audit schedule in Form: AUD002.
Use checklists Form: AUD003/I, Form: AUD003/III, as applicable, for conducting the audit (for guidance, if required).
Use Form: AUD004 to report audit results, which shall also include observations, if any.
Report Non-conformities using Form: NCR001, which shall include time agreed between the auditee and auditor for completion of corrective action on the non-conformity identified. Separate forms shall be used for each non-conformity.
Present a summary of the audit in a closing meeting, which shall include non- conformities and observations.
Hand over audit report to the auditee and send the copy of audit report to the DPA, DO and concerned Group In-charge (Audit report shall consist of Form: AUD002, Form: AUD003, if used, Form: AUD004 and Form: NCR001 and any other comments if made by the auditor).

Non-fulfilment of Classification/Statutory Requirements
During execution of the audit, if any non-fulfilment of Classification/Statutory requirements is observed, same should be immediately brought to the notice of the concerned Group in- charge, Sr. Vice President of the division and the DPA.
Deficiency noted must be corrected immediately, before vessel leaves the port. Master must be suitably advised to take immediate corrective action, as granting of any time frame is not permissible in such a case.

If requisite corrective action has to be deferred for any valid reason, Internal Auditor must confirm that Master/Operating Division immediately approach Classification Society/ Administration to seek such extension. In all such cases, DPA must be kept informed and also as and when corrective action is implemented.

Needless to say, attending superintendent, through survey status and monthly returns from ships, must monitor and ensure that all Class/Statutory surveys, including COC, if any, are planned and completed within the window period. He must also ensure that the ships are complying with all Classifications and Statutory requirements, including SOLAS and MARPOL.

Follow-up on Non-conformities and Observations
Non-conformities identified during the Safety Management System Internal Audit shall be dealt with as shown in the following activity matrices. The auditee shall also take necessary | 
Interview of personnel shall be for the purpose of collecting and noting information. By receiving information from different sources, the auditor shall collate evidence in a precise manner in order to determine conformance to the SMS and possible improvements.
The Internal Safety Management Auditor shall:
Have a meeting with the audit team members, if any, to plan the audit
Have an opening meeting with the Auditee(s), discuss and agree the details of the audit schedule and availability of persons to be interviewed.
Prepare the audit schedule in Form: AUD002.
Use checklists Form: AUD003/I, Form: AUD003/III, as applicable, for conducting the audit (for guidance, if required).
Use Form: AUD004 to report audit results, which shall also include observations, if any.
Report Non-conformities using Form: NCR001, which shall include time agreed between the auditee and auditor for completion of corrective action on the non-conformity identified. Separate forms shall be used for each non-conformity.
Present a summary of the audit in a closing meeting, which shall include non- conformities and observations.
Hand over audit report to the auditee and send the copy of audit report to the DPA, DO and concerned Group In-charge (Audit report shall consist of Form: AUD002, Form: AUD003, if used, Form: AUD004 and Form: NCR001 and any other comments if made by the auditor).

Non-fulfilment of Classification/Statutory Requirements
During execution of the audit, if any non-fulfilment of Classification/Statutory requirements is observed, same should be immediately brought to the notice of the concerned Group in- charge, Sr. Vice President of the division and the DPA.
Deficiency noted must be corrected immediately, before vessel leaves the port. Master must be suitably advised to take immediate corrective action, as granting of any time frame is not permissible in such a case.

If requisite corrective action has to be deferred for any valid reason, Internal Auditor must confirm that Master/Operating Division immediately approach Classification Society/ Administration to seek such extension. In all such cases, DPA must be kept informed and also as and when corrective action is implemented.

Needless to say, attending superintendent, through survey status and monthly returns from ships, must monitor and ensure that all Class/Statutory surveys, including COC, if any, are planned and completed within the window period. He must also ensure that the ships are complying with all Classifications and Statutory requirements, including SOLAS and MARPOL.

Safety Management System External Audit
In compliance with the requirements of the ISM Code, the Company and ships owned/ operated by the Company are subject to DOC and SMC certification/verification external audits by the Administration or the recognised organisations (RO). Procedure for conduct of certification process is detailed below.

Certification, Verification & Control
The Company through the established procedures of the Safety Management System, ensures compliance with the certification process, as per the ISM Code. In doing so, the DPA shall:
Prepare the annual DOC/SMC audit plans for the Company offices, departments and ships and provide a copy of the audit plan to the Departmental Heads, DOs and ISM Coordinators.
Apply and request the Administration or the concerned Authorities for ISM Code certification for the Company and for the ships, including new vessels acquired/taken delivery by the Company, as also ships operated under technical management.
Ensure that the periodical/intermediate and the annual verification are completed before the validity of the DOC and the SMC expire.
If a ship, at the time when her SMC expires, is not in a port where the renewal audit has been planned, the Administration may extend the validity of the SMC to a maximum period of three months. However, this extension shall be granted only for the purpose of allowing the ship to complete her voyage to the port where the audit has been planned.
When SMC Renewal Verification is completed, after the expiry date of the existing SMC, the Administration shall issue new SMC valid from the date of completion of the renewal verification to a date not exceeding 5 years from the date of expiry of existing SMC.
Inform the concerned personnel about the objectives and scope of the ISM Code certification.
Appoint responsible persons to accompany members of the audit team performing the certification.
Provide the resources needed by those performing the certification to ensure an effective and efficient verification process.
Provide access and evidential material as requested by those performing the certification.
Co-operate with the verification team to permit the certification objectives to be achieved.
Initiate follow up of corrective action needed to correct the non-conformity identified during the verification of compliance of SMS for issuance of the DOC and SMC.
The Company should periodically verify whether all those undertaking delegated ISM related tasks are acting in conformity with the Company‘s responsibilities under the code. | Safety Management System External Audit

Review and Evaluation by Management
The efficiency of the SMS shall be periodically evaluated and the SMS shall be reviewed in accordance with the following procedure:
An overall review and evaluation of the Company‘s SMS shall be carried out by the MSPC once in a year. The report with conclusions and recommendations of the review shall be prepared by the DPA. The DPA shall be responsible for monitoring the implementation of any recommendations resulting from the review. He shall maintain the records of such reviews. The DPA shall prepare and organise the review meeting to address all elements of the ISM Code that require management attention. Normally the agenda of the MSPC meeting shall consist at least of the following evaluations:
Implementation of Corrective Actions/Follow-up of Management Review during Last MSPC Meeting.
Results of SMS Annual Internal Audit of the Company and Branch Offices.
Results of last DOC Renewal/Annual/Periodic/Additional Audit.
Summary of Annual Internal SMS Audit of ships.
Results of SMC Interim/Initial/Intermediate/Renewal/Additional Audit of Ships.
Accidents/Hazardous Occurrences Reports and Analysis.
Consideration for updating system in relation to changes in Fleet, Trade, New Regulations and Environmental Requirements.
Various Reports of Inspection and Performance Monitoring.
Status of Compliance with ISPS Code on the Company ships.
Circulars issued.
Forward Plan.
Conclusion and Recommendations.

The DPA shall be responsible for monitoring the implementation of any recommendations resulting from the review. He shall maintain the records of such reviews. The DPA shall prepare and organise the review meeting to address all elements of the ISM Code that require management attention.  | SHIPBOARD SMS MANUAL
Verification, Review & Evaluation | 
Verification and Review

Master‘s Verification
Verification means to investigate and confirm that an activity or operation is in accordance with a specified requirement. (Examples of verification activities include inspections, tests and operational checks on ships and their equipment prior to departing port, at sea or before entering port or closing with the land. A system audit is also an example of a verification activity.)
Master shall implement and verify the shipboard SMS. A Verification Checklist Form: AUD006, along with Form: AUD006(Attachment) has been provided to assist the Master. He may also make additional checklists as required to verify the implementation and effectiveness of the SMS on board the vessel. The verification is a continuous process. On change of Command, the outgoing Master shall hand over the verification record to the incoming Master, who shall continue the verification process and forward the verification report to the Superintendent at the end of each quarter i.e. March, June, October and December.

The Verification Checklist Form: AUD006, along with Form: AUD006(Attachment) gives the elements of SMS, which need to be verified on a continuous basis. Verification shall be conducted in such manner that all aspects of the SMS are covered at least once in every three months. Master shall, as far as practicable, personally carry out the verification process in a cyclic manner by monitoring day to day shipboard operations. Master may assign various verification functions to each member of the Safety Management Team. During the verification, Master shall also sight all logs, records required to be maintained by the SMS, satisfy himself with the compliance of the requirements and sign them as an evidence of his verification process. The passage plans, loading and unloading plans, various checklists, various reports, when made, shall have his approval and signature.

The Verification Checklist Form: AUD006, along with Form: AUD006(Attachment) and comments, if any, shall be forwarded by the Master to the Superintendent responsible for the vessel, with a copy to DO, every three months. The Superintendent/Group I/C shall advise the vessel regarding any follow up action, if required, which might originate from the verification report. A copy of such follow-up action by the Superintendent/Group I/C on the verification report shall be given to DO. A copy of any reports that require DPA‘s action shall be forwarded to him by the DO.

Master‘s Review
Once a year, Master of the vessel shall review all aspects of the shipboard SMS to ensure its continuing suitability and effectiveness in achieving stated objectives. Masters of all vessels shall carry out review once a year from the date of last review, irrespective of period of Command. First review shall be carried out within approximately fifteen days after first Internal Audit. Reviews shall at least include evaluation of the following:
Analysis of NC/Accident/Near Miss and Hazardous Occurrence reports.
SMT/SHEC Reports
